132.s:
īśvara uvāca
sevācakraṃ pravakṣyāmi lābhālābhānusūcakaṃ(2) /
pitā mātā tathā bhrātā dampatī ca viśeṣataḥ //
:n
1 mantraś caiva tu iti kha.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
2 lābhālābhārthasūcakamiti jha.. , ña.. ca
:p 68
132.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
सेवाचक्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि लाभालाभानुसूचकं(2) /
पिता माता तथा भ्राता दम्पती च विशेषतः //
:न्
1 मन्त्रश् चैव तु इति ख.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
2 लाभालाभार्थसूचकमिति झ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 68
132.m:
The Lord said:
I shall explain the Service Wheel, which indicates gain and non-gain
for a father, a mother, and a brother, and especially for a husband and wife.
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: "mantraś caiva tu" in kha.., gha.., ja.., and ña..
2. Variant reading: "lābhālābhārthasūcakam" in jha.. and ña..
[Page 68]

132.s:
tasmiṃś cakre tu vijñeyaṃ yo yasmāllabhate phalaṃ /
ṣaḍūrdhvāḥ sthāpayedrekhā bhinnāścāṣtau tu tiryagāḥ //
132.d:
तस्मिंश् चक्रे तु विज्ञेयं यो यस्माल्लभते फलं /
षडूर्ध्वाः स्थापयेद्रेखा भिन्नाश्चाष्तौ तु तिर्यगाः //
132.m:
In that wheel, it is to be understood who obtains a result from whom.
One should set down six vertical lines and eight distinct crosswise lines.

132.s:
koṣṭhakāḥ pañcatriṃśacca teṣu varṇān samālikhet /
svarān pañca samuddhṛtya sparśān paścāt samālikhet //
132.d:
कोष्ठकाः पञ्चत्रिंशच्च तेषु वर्णान् समालिखेत् /
स्वरान् पञ्च समुद्धृत्य स्पर्शान् पश्चात् समालिखेत् //
132.m:
There are thirty-five compartments; in them one should write the letters.
Having drawn out the five vowels, one should afterward write the consonants.

132.s:
kakārādihakārāntān hīnāṅgāṃstrīnvivarjayet /
siddhaḥ sādhyaḥ susiddhaś ca arirmṛtyuś ca nāmataḥ //
132.d:
ककारादिहकारान्तान् हीनाङ्गांस्त्रीन्विवर्जयेत् /
सिद्धः साध्यः सुसिद्धश् च अरिर्मृत्युश् च नामतः //
132.m:
Beginning with "ka" and ending with "ha", one should omit the three deficient letters.
They are named: the accomplished, the to-be-accomplished, the well-accomplished, the enemy, and death.

132.s:
arirmṛtyuaś ca dvāvetau varjayet sarvakarmasu /
eṣāṃ madhye yadā nāma lakṣayettu prayatnataḥ //
132.d:
अरिर्मृत्युअश् च द्वावेतौ वर्जयेत् सर्वकर्मसु /
एषां मध्ये यदा नाम लक्षयेत्तु प्रयत्नतः //
132.m:
One should avoid both the enemy and death in all undertakings.
When one examines a name among these with effort,

132.s:
ātmapakṣe(1) sthitāḥ sattvāḥ sarve te śubhadāyakāḥ /
dvitīyaḥ poṣakāś caiva tṛtīyaścārthadāyakaḥ //
132.d:
आत्मपक्षे(1) स्थिताः सत्त्वाः सर्वे ते शुभदायकाः /
द्वितीयः पोषकाश् चैव तृतीयश्चार्थदायकः //
132.m:
all the beings situated on one's own side grant what is auspicious.
The second is nourishing, and the third brings wealth;

132.s:
ātmanāśaś caturthastu(2) pañcamo mṛtyudāyakaḥ /
sthānamevārthalābhāya mitrabhṛtyādivāndhavāḥ //
132.d:
आत्मनाशश् चतुर्थस्तु(2) पञ्चमो मृत्युदायकः /
स्थानमेवार्थलाभाय मित्रभृत्यादिवान्धवाः //
132.m:
the fourth is destruction of oneself, and the fifth brings death.
Friends, servants, relatives, and others [are tested] for obtaining wealth from a place.

132.s:
siddhaḥ sādhyaḥ susiddhaś ca sarve te phaladāyakāḥ /
arirbhṛtyaś ca dvāvetau varjayet sarvakarmasu(3) //
132.d:
सिद्धः साध्यः सुसिद्धश् च सर्वे ते फलदायकाः /
अरिर्भृत्यश् च द्वावेतौ वर्जयेत् सर्वकर्मसु(3) //
132.m:
The accomplished, the to-be-accomplished, and the well-accomplished—all of them bestow fruits.
Both the enemy and the servant one should avoid in all undertakings.

132.s:
akārāntaṃ yathā proktaṃ a+i+u+e+o vidus tathā /
punaś caivāṃśakān vakṣye vargāṣṭakasusaṃskṛtān //
132.d:
अकारान्तं यथा प्रोक्तं अ+इ+उ+ए+ओ विदुस् तथा /
पुनश् चैवांशकान् वक्ष्ये वर्गाष्टकसुसंस्कृतान् //
132.m:
As is taught ending with "a", the wise know them thus: a, i, u, e, o.
Moreover, I shall declare the portions properly prepared by the eight classes [of letters]:

132.s:
devā akāravarge daityāḥ kavargamāśritāḥ /
nāgāś caiva cavargāḥ syurgandhavāś ca ṭavargajāḥ //
:n
1 svārthapakṣe iti kha.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca / svātmapakṣe iti jha..
2 svārthanāśaś caturthastu iti kha.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
3 arirmṛtyurityādiḥ, sarvakarmasu ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ cha.. pustake
nāsti
:p 69
132.d:
देवा अकारवर्गे दैत्याः कवर्गमाश्रिताः /
नागाश् चैव चवर्गाः स्युर्गन्धवाश् च टवर्गजाः //
:न्
1 स्वार्थपक्षे इति ख.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च / स्वात्मपक्षे इति झ..
2 स्वार्थनाशश् चतुर्थस्तु इति ख.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
3 अरिर्मृत्युरित्यादिः, सर्वकर्मसु इत्य् अन्तः पाठः छ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 69
132.m:
the gods reside in the "a"-class, the daityas belong to the "ka"-class,
the nāgas belong to the "ca"-class, and the gandharvas are born of the "ṭa"-class;
[Footnote]
1. Variant reading: "svārthapakṣe" in kha.., gha.., ja.., ña..; "svātmapakṣe" in jha..
2. Variant reading: "svārthanāśaś caturthastu" in kha.., gha.., ṅa.., ja.., ña..
3. The passage from "arirmṛtyu..." up to "...sarvakarmasu" is absent in manuscript cha..
[Page 69]

132.s:
tavarge ṛṣayaḥ proktāḥ pavarge rākṣasāḥ smṛtāḥ /
piśācāś ca yavarge ca śavarge mānuṣāḥ smṛtāḥ //
132.d:
तवर्गे ऋषयः प्रोक्ताः पवर्गे राक्षसाः स्मृताः /
पिशाचाश् च यवर्गे च शवर्गे मानुषाः स्मृताः //
132.m:
the ṛṣis are taught in the "ta"-class, the rākṣasas are remembered in the "pa"-class,
the piśācas in the "ya"-class, and mortals are remembered in the "śa"-class.

132.s:
devebhyo balino daityā daityebhyaḥ pannagās tathā(1) /
pannagebhyaś ca gandharvā gandharvādṛṣayo varāḥ //
132.d:
देवेभ्यो बलिनो दैत्या दैत्येभ्यः पन्नगास् तथा(1) /
पन्नगेभ्यश् च गन्धर्वा गन्धर्वादृषयो वराः //
132.m:
The daityas are stronger than the gods, and serpents are stronger than the daityas;
the gandharvas are stronger than serpents, and the ṛṣis are superior to the gandharvas;

132.s:
ṛṣibhyo rākṣasāḥ śūrā rākṣasebhyaḥ piśācakāḥ /
piśācebhyo mānuṣāḥ syurdurbalaṃ varjayedbalī //
132.d:
ऋषिभ्यो राक्षसाः शूरा राक्षसेभ्यः पिशाचकाः /
पिशाचेभ्यो मानुषाः स्युर्दुर्बलं वर्जयेद्बली //
132.m:
the rākṣasas are braver than the ṛṣis, and the piśācas are stronger than the rākṣasas;
mortals are superior to the piśācas: the strong should avoid the weak.

132.s:
punarmitravibhāgantu tārācakraṃ kramācchṛṇu /
nāmādyakṣaramṛkṣantu sphuṭaṃ kṛtvā tu parvataḥ //
132.d:
पुनर्मित्रविभागन्तु ताराचक्रं क्रमाच्छृणु /
नामाद्यक्षरमृक्षन्तु स्फुटं कृत्वा तु पर्वतः //
132.m:
Now listen in order to the Asterism Wheel for distinguishing friends.
Having ascertained the asterism from the first letter of the name, O Mountain,

132.s:
ṛkṣe tu saṃsthitāstārā navatrikā yathākramāt /
janma sampadvipat kṣemaṃ nāmarkṣāttārakā imāḥ //
132.d:
ऋक्षे तु संस्थितास्तारा नवत्रिका यथाक्रमात् /
जन्म सम्पद्विपत् क्षेमं नामर्क्षात्तारका इमाः //
132.m:
the asterisms situated in the constellation are three triads of nine, in due order:
birth, prosperity, calamity, safety—these are the asterisms from the name-asterism;

132.s:
pratyarā dhanadā ṣaṣṭhī naidhanāmaitrake pare /
paramaitrāntimā tārā janmatārā tvaśobhanā //
132.d:
प्रत्यरा धनदा षष्ठी नैधनामैत्रके परे /
परमैत्रान्तिमा तारा जन्मतारा त्वशोभना //
132.m:
the sixth is adversarial, wealth-giving; the next two are lethal and friendly;
the final asterism is extremely friendly, while the birth asterism is inauspicious;

132.s:
sampattārā mahāśreṣṭhā vipattārā tu niṣphalā /
kṣematārā sarvakārye pratparā arthanāśinī(2) //
132.d:
सम्पत्तारा महाश्रेष्ठा विपत्तारा तु निष्फला /
क्षेमतारा सर्वकार्ये प्रत्परा अर्थनाशिनी(2) //
132.m:
the prosperity asterism is most excellent, but the calamity asterism is fruitless;
the safety asterism [is good] in every task; the adversarial asterism destroys wealth.

132.s:
dhanadā rājyalābhādi naidhanā kāryanāśinī /
maitratārā ca mitrāya paramitrā hitāvahā(3) //
132.d:
धनदा राज्यलाभादि नैधना कार्यनाशिनी /
मैत्रतारा च मित्राय परमित्रा हितावहा(3) //
132.m: The Dhanadā gives acquisition of a kingdom and the like; the Naidhanā ruins undertakings. / The Maitra star brings friendship, and the Paramamaitra brings welfare.

132.s:
tārācakraṃ |mātrā vai svarasañjñā syānnāmamadhye kṣipet priye /
viṃśatyā ca haredbhāgaṃ yaccheṣaṃ tat phalaṃ bhavet //
132.d:
ताराचक्रं |मात्रा वै स्वरसञ्ज्ञा स्यान्नाममध्ये क्षिपेत् प्रिये /
विंशत्या च हरेद्भागं यच्छेषं तत् फलं भवेत् //
132.m: The circle of asterisms. A mora is designated as a vowel; one should add it in the middle of a name, O dear one. / One should divide the sum by twenty; whatever is the remainder, that becomes the result.

132.s:
ubhayortrāsamadhye tu lakṣayecca dhanaṃ hy ṛṇaṃ /
hīnamātrā hy ṛṇaṃ jñeyandhanaṃ mātrādhikaṃ punaḥ //
:n
1 pannagāstatra iti ka.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca / pannagāḥ smṛtā iti
jha..
2 pratyarā cātmanāśinī iti cha..
3 hitāya ceti ṅa..
:p 70
132.d:
उभयोर्त्रासमध्ये तु लक्षयेच्च धनं ह्य् ऋणं /
हीनमात्रा ह्य् ऋणं ज्ञेयन्धनं मात्राधिकं पुनः //
:न्
1 पन्नगास्तत्र इति क.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च / पन्नगाः स्मृता इति
झ..
2 प्रत्यरा चात्मनाशिनी इति छ..
3 हिताय चेति ङ..
:प् 70
132.m:
Between the two persons, one should observe wealth and debt: / fewer morae should be known as debt, whereas more morae [denotes] wealth.
[Footnote]
1. "pannagās tatra" according to manuscripts ka, ga, gha, ṅa, and ña. / "pannagāḥ smṛtāḥ" according to manuscript jha.
2. "pratyarā cātmanāśinī" according to manuscript cha.
3. "hitāya ca" according to manuscript ṅa.
[Page 70]

132.s:
dhanena mitratā nṝṇāṃ ṛṇenaiva hy udāsatā /
sevācakramidaṃ proktaṃ lābhālābhādidarśakaṃ //
132.d:
धनेन मित्रता नॄणां ऋणेनैव ह्य् उदासता /
सेवाचक्रमिदं प्रोक्तं लाभालाभादिदर्शकं //
132.m: By wealth arises friendship among men; by debt alone arises indifference. / This sevācakra has been taught, showing gain, loss, and the like.

132.s:
meṣamithunayoḥ prītirmaitrī mithunasiṃhayoḥ /
tulāsiṃhau mahāmaitrī evaṃ dhanurghaṭe punaḥ //
132.d:
मेषमिथुनयोः प्रीतिर्मैत्री मिथुनसिंहयोः /
तुलासिंहौ महामैत्री एवं धनुर्घटे पुनः //
132.m: Affection exists between Aries and Gemini, and friendship between Gemini and Leo; / Libra and Leo have great friendship; likewise Sagittarius and Aquarius.

132.s:
mitrasevāṃ na kurvīta mitrau mīnavṛṣau matau /
vṛṣakarkaṭayormaitrī kulīraghaṭayos tathā //
132.d:
मित्रसेवां न कुर्वीत मित्रौ मीनवृषौ मतौ /
वृषकर्कटयोर्मैत्री कुलीरघटयोस् तथा //
132.m: One should not render service to a friend; Pisces and Taurus are considered friends. / Friendship exists between Taurus and Cancer, and likewise between Cancer and Aquarius;

132.s:
kanyāvṛścikayorevantathā makarakīṭayoḥ /
mīnamakarayormaitrī tṛtīyaikādaśe sthitā //
132.d:
कन्यावृश्चिकयोरेवन्तथा मकरकीटयोः /
मीनमकरयोर्मैत्री तृतीयैकादशे स्थिता //
132.m: likewise between Virgo and Scorpio, and between Capricorn and Scorpio. / Friendship exists between Pisces and Capricorn, standing in the third and eleventh [houses].

132.s:
tulāmeṣau mahāmaitrī vidviṣṭo vṛṣavṛścikau /
mithunadhanuṣoḥ prītiḥ karkaṭamakarayos tathā //
132.d:
तुलामेषौ महामैत्री विद्विष्टो वृषवृश्चिकौ /
मिथुनधनुषोः प्रीतिः कर्कटमकरयोस् तथा //
132.m: Libra and Aries have great friendship; Taurus and Scorpio are hostile; / affection exists between Gemini and Sagittarius, and likewise between Cancer and Capricorn;

132.s:
mṛgakumbhakayoḥ prītiḥ kanāmīnau tathaiva ca //26//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave sevācakraṃ nāma
dvātriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha trayastriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānābalāni
132.d:
मृगकुम्भकयोः प्रीतिः कनामीनौ तथैव च //26//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे सेवाचक्रं नाम
द्वात्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानाबलानि
132.m:
affection exists between Capricorn and Aquarius, and likewise between Virgo and Pisces.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-second chapter, called the Sevācakra, in the Yuddhajayārṇava in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the one hundred and thirty-third chapter.
Various strengths.

133.s:
īśvara uvāca
garbhajātasya vakṣyāmi kṣetrādhipasvarūpakaṃ /
nātidīrghaḥ kṛśaḥ sthūlaḥ samāṅgo gaurapaitikaḥ //
:p 71
133.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
गर्भजातस्य वक्ष्यामि क्षेत्राधिपस्वरूपकं /
नातिदीर्घः कृशः स्थूलः समाङ्गो गौरपैतिकः //
:प् 71
133.m:
The Lord said: / I shall declare the nature of the lord of the sign for one born from the womb: / not too tall, thin or stout, having symmetrical limbs, fair, of bilious constitution,
[Page 71]

133.s:
raktākṣo guṇavān śūro gṛhe sūryasya jāyate /
saubhāgyo mṛdusāraś ca jātaś candragṛhodaye //
133.d:
रक्ताक्षो गुणवान् शूरो गृहे सूर्यस्य जायते /
सौभाग्यो मृदुसारश् च जातश् चन्द्रगृहोदये //
133.m: red-eyed, virtuous, and heroic is one born in the house of the Sun. / One born in the rising house of the Moon is fortunate, mild, and strong.

133.s:
vātādhiko 'tilubdhādirjāto bhūmibhuvo gṛhe /
buddhimān subhago mānī jātaḥ saumyagṛhodaye //
133.d:
वाताधिको ऽतिलुब्धादिर्जातो भूमिभुवो गृहे /
बुद्धिमान् सुभगो मानी जातः सौम्यगृहोदये //
133.m: One born in the house of the son of the Earth (Mars) has an excess of wind, is exceedingly greedy, and the like. / One born in the rising house of Mercury is intelligent, fortunate, and proud.

133.s:
vṛhatkrodhaś ca śubhago jāto gurugṛhe naraḥ /
tyāgo bhogo ca subhago jāto bhṛgugṛhodaye //
133.d:
वृहत्क्रोधश् च शुभगो जातो गुरुगृहे नरः /
त्यागो भोगो च सुभगो जातो भृगुगृहोदये //
133.m: A man born in the house of Jupiter has great wrath and is fortunate. / One born in the rising house of Venus possesses renunciation and enjoyment, and is fortunate.

133.s:
buddhimāñchubhago mānī jātaścārkigṛhe naraḥ /
saumyalagne tu saumyaḥ syāt krūraḥ syāt krūralagnake //
133.d:
बुद्धिमाञ्छुभगो मानी जातश्चार्किगृहे नरः /
सौम्यलग्ने तु सौम्यः स्यात् क्रूरः स्यात् क्रूरलग्नके //
133.m: A man born in the house of Saturn is intelligent, fortunate, and proud. / In a gentle ascendant one becomes gentle; in a cruel ascendant one becomes cruel.

133.s:
daśāphalaṅgauri vakṣye nāmarāśau tu saṃsthitaṃ /
gajāśvadhanadhānyāni rājyaśrīrvipulā bhavet //
133.d:
दशाफलङ्गौरि वक्ष्ये नामराशौ तु संस्थितं /
गजाश्वधनधान्यानि राज्यश्रीर्विपुला भवेत् //
133.m: O Gaurī, I shall declare the result of the planetary period standing in the sign of the name: / Elephants, horses, wealth, and grain, and vast royal splendor arise;

133.s:
punardhanāgamaścāpi daśāyāṃ bhāskarasya tu /
divyastrīdā candradaśā bhūmilābhaḥ sukhaṃ kuje //
133.d:
पुनर्धनागमश्चापि दशायां भास्करस्य तु /
दिव्यस्त्रीदा चन्द्रदशा भूमिलाभः सुखं कुजे //
133.m: and also the arrival of wealth again, in the planetary period of the Sun. / The period of the Moon bestows divine women; in that of Mars there is acquisition of land and happiness.

133.s:
bhūmirdhānyaṃ dhanaṃ baudhe gajāśvādidhanaṃ gurau /
khādyapānadhanaṃ dśukre śanau vyādhyādisaṃyutaḥ //
133.d:
भूमिर्धान्यं धनं बौधे गजाश्वादिधनं गुरौ /
खाद्यपानधनं द्शुक्रे शनौ व्याध्यादिसंयुतः //
133.m: In that of Mercury there is land, grain, and wealth; in that of Jupiter, wealth such as elephants and horses; / in that of Venus, wealth, food, and drink; in that of Saturn, one is afflicted with diseases and the like.

133.s:
snānasevādinādhvānaṃ vāṇijyaṃ rāhurdarśane /
vāmanāḍīpravāhe syānnāma cedviṣamākṣaraṃ //
133.d:
स्नानसेवादिनाध्वानं वाणिज्यं राहुर्दर्शने /
वामनाडीप्रवाहे स्यान्नाम चेद्विषमाक्षरं //
133.m: On seeing Rāhu, travel [brings] bathing, service, and trade. / When the flow is in the left channel, if the name has an odd number of syllables,

133.s:
tadā jayati saṅgrāme śanibhaumasasaiṃhikāḥ /
dakṣanāḍīpravāherke vāṇijye caiva niṣphalā //
133.d:
तदा जयति सङ्ग्रामे शनिभौमससैंहिकाः /
दक्षनाडीप्रवाहेर्के वाणिज्ये चैव निष्फला //
133.m: then Saturn, Mars, and Rāhu conquer in battle. / When the flow is in the right channel during the Sun, it is fruitless in trade.

133.s:
saṅgrāme jayamāpnoti samanāmā naro dhruvaṃ /
adhaścāre jayaṃ vidyādūrdhvacāre raṇe mṛtiṃ //
oṃ hūṃ oṃ hrūṃ oṃ spheṃ astraṃ moṭaya(1) oṃ cūrṇaya 2
oṃ sarvaśatruṃ mardaya 2 oṃ hrūṃ oṃ hraḥ phaṭ
:n
1 mocayeti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 72
133.d:
सङ्ग्रामे जयमाप्नोति समनामा नरो ध्रुवं /
अधश्चारे जयं विद्यादूर्ध्वचारे रणे मृतिं //
ओं हूं ओं ह्रूं ओं स्फें अस्त्रं मोटय(1) ओं चूर्णय 2
ओं सर्वशत्रुं मर्दय 2 ओं ह्रूं ओं ह्रः फट्
:न्
1 मोचयेति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 72
133.m:
A man whose name has an even number of syllables surely attains victory in battle. / One should know victory in a downward flow, and death in battle in an upward flow.
Oṃ hūṃ oṃ hrūṃ oṃ spheṃ, break the weapon! Oṃ crush, crush! / Oṃ crush all enemies, crush! Oṃ hrūṃ oṃ hraḥ phaṭ!
[Footnote]
1. "mocaya" according to manuscripts kha and cha.
[Page 72]

133.s:
saptavārannyasenmantraṃ dhyātvātmānantu bhair avaṃ /
caturbhujandaśabhujaṃ viṃśadbāhvātmakaṃ śubhaṃ //
133.d:
सप्तवारन्न्यसेन्मन्त्रं ध्यात्वात्मानन्तु भैर् अवं /
चतुर्भुजन्दशभुजं विंशद्बाह्वात्मकं शुभं //
133.m: One should apply the mantra seven times, meditating upon oneself as Bhairava: / having four arms, ten arms, or having twenty arms, auspicious,

133.s:
śūlakhaṭvāṅgahastantu khaḍgakaṭṭārikodyataṃ /
bhakṣaṇaṃ parasainyānāmātmasainyaparāṅmukhaṃ //
133.d:
शूलखट्वाङ्गहस्तन्तु खड्गकट्टारिकोद्यतं /
भक्षणं परसैन्यानामात्मसैन्यपराङ्मुखं //
133.m: bearing a trident and a skull-topped staff in the hands, raising a sword and a dagger, / devouring the armies of the enemy, turning away from one's own army,

133.s:
sammukhaṃ śatrasainyasya śatamaṣṭottaraṃ japet /
japāḍḍamarukācchabdācchastraṃ tyaktvā palāyate //
133.d:
सम्मुखं शत्रसैन्यस्य शतमष्टोत्तरं जपेत् /
जपाड्डमरुकाच्छब्दाच्छस्त्रं त्यक्त्वा पलायते //
133.m: facing the army of the enemy. One should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times. / From the recitation and from the sound of the damaru, [the enemy] flees, casting away weapons.

133.s:
parasainyaṃ śṛṇu bhaṅgaṃ prayogena punarvade /
śmaśānāṅgāramādāya viṣṭāñcolūkakākayoḥ //
133.d:
परसैन्यं शृणु भङ्गं प्रयोगेन पुनर्वदे /
श्मशानाङ्गारमादाय विष्टाञ्चोलूककाकयोः //
133.m: Hear the rout of the enemy army; I shall explain it again by means of a rite: / Taking charcoal from a cremation ground and the excrement of an owl and a crow,

133.s:
karpaṭe pratimāṃ likhya sādhyastaivākṣaraṃ yathā /
nāmātha navadhā likhya ripoś caiva yathākramaṃ //
133.d:
कर्पटे प्रतिमां लिख्य साध्यस्तैवाक्षरं यथा /
नामाथ नवधा लिख्य रिपोश् चैव यथाक्रमं //
133.m: drawing an effigy on a rag, just as the syllables [of the name] of the target [are written], / one should write the name of the enemy ninefold in due order:

133.s:
mūrdhni vaktre lalāṭe ca hṛdaye guhyapādayoḥ /
pṛṣṭhe tu bāhumadhye tu(1) nāma vai navadhā likhet //
133.d:
मूर्ध्नि वक्त्रे ललाटे च हृदये गुह्यपादयोः /
पृष्ठे तु बाहुमध्ये तु(1) नाम वै नवधा लिखेत् //
133.m: on the crown of the head, on the face, on the forehead, on the heart, on the privities, and on the feet, / on the back, and between the arms—one should write the name ninefold.

133.s:
moṭayedyuddhakāle tu(2) uccaritvā tu vidyaya /
tārkṣyacakraṃ pravakṣyāmi jayārthaṃ trimukhākṣaraṃ(3) //
133.d:
मोटयेद्युद्धकाले तु(2) उच्चरित्वा तु विद्यय /
तार्क्ष्यचक्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि जयार्थं त्रिमुखाक्षरं(3) //
133.m: One should crush it at the time of battle, having recited it with the incantation. / I shall declare the Tārkṣya-cakra of three-faced syllables for the sake of victory.

133.s:
kṣipa oṃ svāhā tārkṣātmā śatrurogaviṣādinut /
duṣṭabhūtagrahārtasya vyādhitasyāturasya ca //
133.d:
क्षिप ओं स्वाहा तार्क्षात्मा शत्रुरोगविषादिनुत् /
दुष्टभूतग्रहार्तस्य व्याधितस्यातुरस्य च //
133.m: “Kṣipa oṃ svāhā”—the one whose self is Tārkṣya dispels enemies, diseases, poisons, and the like. / For one afflicted by evil spirits and malignant planets, for the diseased and the suffering,

133.s:
karoti yādṛśaṅkarma tādṛśaṃ siddhyate khagāt /
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamañcaiva lūtāś ca kṛtrimaṃ viṣaṃ //
133.d:
करोति यादृशङ्कर्म तादृशं सिद्ध्यते खगात् /
स्थावरं जङ्गमञ्चैव लूताश् च कृत्रिमं विषं //
133.m: whatever rite one performs, such succeeds through the bird (Garuḍa). / Stationary and mobile poisons, spider venom, and artificial poison—

133.s:
tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti(4) sādhakasyāvalokanāt /
:n
1 bāhumūle tu iti ga..
2 mocayedyuddhakāle tu iti ja.. , jha.. ca
3 jayārthaṃ bhūmukhākṣaramiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja..
ca
4 nāśamāpnotīti ja..
:p 73
punardhyāyenmahātārkṣyaṃ dvipakṣaṃ mānuṣākṛtiṃ //
133.d:
तत्सर्वं नाशमायाति(4) साधकस्यावलोकनात् /
:न्
1 बाहुमूले तु इति ग..
2 मोचयेद्युद्धकाले तु इति ज.. , झ.. च
3 जयार्थं भूमुखाक्षरमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज..
च
4 नाशमाप्नोतीति ज..
:प् 73
पुनर्ध्यायेन्महातार्क्ष्यं द्विपक्षं मानुषाकृतिं //
133.m:
all that goes to destruction merely by the glance of the practitioner.
[Footnote]
1. "bāhumūle tu" according to manuscript ga.
2. "mocayed yuddhakāle tu" according to manuscripts ja and jha.
3. "jayārthaṃ bhūmukhākṣaram" according to manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, and ja.
4. "nāśam āpnoti" according to manuscript ja.
[Page 73]
Furthermore, one should meditate upon great Tārkṣya having two wings and a human form,

133.s:
dvibhujaṃ vakracañcuṃ ca(1) gajakūrmadharaṃ prabhuṃ /
asaṅkhyoragapādasthamāgacchantaṃ khamadhyataḥ //
133.d:
द्विभुजं वक्रचञ्चुं च(1) गजकूर्मधरं प्रभुं /
असङ्ख्योरगपादस्थमागच्छन्तं खमध्यतः //
133.m: two-armed, with a curved beak, the lord bearing an elephant and a tortoise, / standing upon feet of innumerable serpents, descending from the midst of the sky,

133.s:
grasantañcaiva khādantaṃ tudantaṃ cāhave ripūn /
cañcvāhatāś ca draṣṭavyāḥ kecitpādaiś ca cūrṇitāḥ //
133.d:
ग्रसन्तञ्चैव खादन्तं तुदन्तं चाहवे रिपून् /
चञ्च्वाहताश् च द्रष्टव्याः केचित्पादैश् च चूर्णिताः //
133.m: swallowing, devouring, and striking the enemies in battle. / Some are to be visualized struck by his beak, others crushed by his feet,

133.s:
pakṣapātaiścūrṇitāś ca kecinnaṣṭā diśo daśa /
tārkṣyadhyānānvito yaś ca trilokye hy ajayo bhavet(2) //
133.d:
पक्षपातैश्चूर्णिताश् च केचिन्नष्टा दिशो दश /
तार्क्ष्यध्यानान्वितो यश् च त्रिलोक्ये ह्य् अजयो भवेत्(2) //
133.m: and others crushed by the blows of his wings, while some flee in the ten directions. / And he who is endowed with meditation on Tārkṣya becomes invincible in the three worlds.

133.s:
picchikāntu pravakṣyāmi mantrasādhanajāṃ kriyāṃ /
oṃ hrūṃ pakṣin kṣipa oṃ hūṃ saḥ mahābalaparākrama
sarvasainyaṃ bhakṣaya 2 oṃ mardaya 2 oṃ cūrṇaya 2 oṃ vidrāvaya 2
oṃ hūṃ khaḥ oṃ bhairavo jñāpayati svāhā
amuñcandragrahaṇe tu japaṅkṛtvā tu picchikāṃ //
133.d:
पिच्छिकान्तु प्रवक्ष्यामि मन्त्रसाधनजां क्रियां /
ओं ह्रूं पक्षिन् क्षिप ओं हूं सः महाबलपराक्रम
सर्वसैन्यं भक्षय 2 ओं मर्दय 2 ओं चूर्णय 2 ओं विद्रावय 2
ओं हूं खः ओं भैरवो ज्ञापयति स्वाहा
अमुञ्चन्द्रग्रहणे तु जपङ्कृत्वा तु पिच्छिकां //
133.m:
I shall declare the [use of the] peacock-feather brush, a rite born of mantra mastery:
“Oṃ hrūṃ, O bird, strike! Oṃ hūṃ saḥ, O one of great strength and prowess, devour the entire army, devour! Oṃ crush, crush! Oṃ shatter, shatter! Oṃ put to flight, put to flight! Oṃ hūṃ khaḥ, Bhairava commands, svāhā!”
Having performed recitation of this during a lunar eclipse, [holding] the peacock-feather brush,

133.s:
mantrayed bhrāmayetsainyaṃ sammukhaṃ gajasiṃhayoḥ /
dhyānādravān mardayecca siṃhārūḍho mṛgāvikān //
133.d:
मन्त्रयेद् भ्रामयेत्सैन्यं सम्मुखं गजसिंहयोः /
ध्यानाद्रवान् मर्दयेच्च सिंहारूढो मृगाविकान् //
133.m: one should consecrate it and wave it before the army against elephants and lions. / By meditation, one mounted on a lion would crush the deer and sheep from their roar.

133.s:
śabdādbhaṅgaṃ pravakṣyāmi dūraṃ mantreṇa(3) bodhayet /
mātṝṇāṃ carukaṃ dadyāt kālarātryā viśeṣataḥ //
133.d:
शब्दाद्भङ्गं प्रवक्ष्यामि दूरं मन्त्रेण(3) बोधयेत् /
मातॄणां चरुकं दद्यात् कालरात्र्या विशेषतः //
133.m: I shall declare rout by sound; one should frighten [the enemy] from afar with a mantra. / One should offer an oblation of boiled rice to the Mothers, especially to Kālarātrī.

133.s:
śmaśānabhasmasaṃyuktaṃ mālatī cāmarī tathā(4) /
kārpāsamūlamātrantu tena dūrantu bodhayet //
oṃ ahe he mahendri ahe mahendri bhañja hi oṃ jahi masānaṃhi khāhi
khāhi kili kili kili oṃ huṃ phaṭ
:n
1 vajracañcuṃ ceti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 abhayo bhavediti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. ca
3 haramantreṇeti ka.. / mūlamantreṇeti kha.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
4 mālatī vānarī tatheti cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 74
133.d:
श्मशानभस्मसंयुक्तं मालती चामरी तथा(4) /
कार्पासमूलमात्रन्तु तेन दूरन्तु बोधयेत् //
ओं अहे हे महेन्द्रि अहे महेन्द्रि भञ्ज हि ओं जहि मसानंहि खाहि
खाहि किलि किलि किलि ओं हुं फट्
:न्
1 वज्रचञ्चुं चेति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 अभयो भवेदिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. च
3 हरमन्त्रेणेति क.. / मूलमन्त्रेणेति ख.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
4 मालती वानरी तथेति छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 74
133.m:
Mixed with ashes from a cremation ground, jasmine, a yak-tail whisk, / and just the root of a cotton plant, with that one should frighten [them] from afar:
“Oṃ ahe he Mahendrī, ahe Mahendrī, break! Oṃ kill! Eat in the cremation ground, eat! Kili kili kili, oṃ huṃ phaṭ!”
[Footnote]
1. "vajracañcuṃ ca" according to manuscripts ga, gha, ṅa, and ña.
[Variant reading:] "abhayo bhavet" in MSS ga, gha, and ṅa.
[Variant reading:] "haramantreṇa" in MS ka; "mūlamantreṇa" in MSS kha, gha, ja, and ña.
[Variant reading:] "mālatī vānarī tathā" in MSS cha and ña.

133.s:
arer nāśaṃ dūraśabdājjaptayā bhaṅgavidyayā /
aparājitā ca dhustūrastābhyāntu tilakena hi //
oṃ kili kili vikili icchākili bhūtahani śaṅkhini ubhe daṇdahaste raudri
māheśvari ulkāmukhi jvālāmukhi śaṅkukarṇe śuṣkajaṅghe
alambuṣe hara oṃ sarvaduṣṭān khana oṃ yanmannirīkṣayeddevi
tāṃstān mohaya oṃ rudrasya hṛdaye sthitā raudri saumyena bhāvena
ātmarakṣāntataḥ kuru svāhā
133.d:
अरेर् नाशं दूरशब्दाज्जप्तया भङ्गविद्यया /
अपराजिता च धुस्तूरस्ताभ्यान्तु तिलकेन हि //
ओं किलि किलि विकिलि इच्छाकिलि भूतहनि शङ्खिनि उभे दण्दहस्ते रौद्रि
माहेश्वरि उल्कामुखि ज्वालामुखि शङ्कुकर्णे शुष्कजङ्घे
अलम्बुषे हर ओं सर्वदुष्टान् खन ओं यन्मन्निरीक्षयेद्देवि
तांस्तान् मोहय ओं रुद्रस्य हृदये स्थिता रौद्रि सौम्येन भावेन
आत्मरक्षान्ततः कुरु स्वाहा
133.m:
The destruction of the enemy [occurs] through the spell of routing, recited from a distance. / Aparājitā and dhustūra, indeed, [are used] for a forehead mark with both of them.
"Oṃ kili kili vikili, O one who binds at will, slayer of spirits, śaṅkhinī, both carrying a staff in hand, fierce one, / O Māheśvarī, meteor-faced, flame-faced, peg-eared, dry-shinned, / Alambuṣā, destroy! Oṃ, dig out all wicked ones! Oṃ, O goddess, whomever he might gaze upon, / delude all of them! Oṃ, O fierce one abiding in the heart of Rudra, with a gentle disposition / make protection of the self thereafter, svāhā!"

133.s:
vāhyato mātṝḥ saṃlikhya sakalākṛtiveṣṭitāḥ /
nāgapatre(1) likhedvidyāṃ sarvakāmārthasādhanīṃ //
133.d:
वाह्यतो मातॄः संलिख्य सकलाकृतिवेष्टिताः /
नागपत्रे(1) लिखेद्विद्यां सर्वकामार्थसाधनीं //
133.m: Having inscribed the Mothers on the outside, enveloped in all forms, / one should write the spell that accomplishes all desires and aims upon a betel leaf.

133.s:
hastādyair dhāritā pūrvaṃ brahmarudrendraviṣṇubhiḥ /
gurusaṅgrāmakāle tu vidyayā rakṣitāḥ surāḥ //
133.d:
हस्ताद्यैर् धारिता पूर्वं ब्रह्मरुद्रेन्द्रविष्णुभिः /
गुरुसङ्ग्रामकाले तु विद्यया रक्षिताः सुराः //
133.m: It was formerly worn on the arm and other limbs by Brahmā, Rudra, Indra, and Viṣṇu; / at the time of great battle, indeed, the gods were protected by the spell.

133.s:
rakṣayā nārasiṃhyā ca bhairavyā śaktirūpayā /
sarve trailokyamohinyā gauryā devāsure raṇe //
133.d:
रक्षया नारसिंह्या च भैरव्या शक्तिरूपया /
सर्वे त्रैलोक्यमोहिन्या गौर्या देवासुरे रणे //
133.m: All [the gods were protected] in the battle between gods and demons by the protective spell of Nārasiṃhī, / by Bhairavī in the form of Śakti, and by Gaurī, the deluder of the three worlds.

133.s:
vījasampuṭitaṃ nāma karṇikāyāṃ daleṣu ca /
pūjākrameṇa cāṅgāni rakṣāyantraṃ(2) smṛtaṃ śubhe //
133.d:
वीजसम्पुटितं नाम कर्णिकायां दलेषु च /
पूजाक्रमेण चाङ्गानि रक्षायन्त्रं(2) स्मृतं शुभे //
133.m: The name, enclosed within the seed-syllables, in the pericarp and on the petals, / and the subsidiary limbs according to the sequence of worship—this is considered the protective yantra, O auspicious lady.

133.s:
mṛtyuñjayaṃ pravakṣyāmi nāmasaṃskāramadhyaga /
kalābhiveṣṭitaṃ paścāt sakāreṇa nibodhitaṃ //
133.d:
मृत्युञ्जयं प्रवक्ष्यामि नामसंस्कारमध्यग /
कलाभिवेष्टितं पश्चात् सकारेण निबोधितं //
133.m: I shall proclaim the Mṛtyuñjaya [yantra], situated in the midst of the consecration of the name, / enveloped by the Kalās, subsequently awakened by the syllable "sa",

133.s:
jakāraṃ vindusaṃyuktaṃ oṅkāreṇa samanvitaṃ /
dhakārodaramadhyasthaṃ vakāreṇa nibodhitaṃ(3) //
:n
1 nāgayantre iti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 rakṣāmantramiti kha.. , ga.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca
3 kakārodaramadhyasthaṃ cakāreṇeti kha.. / cakārodaramadhyasthaṃ
cakāreṇeti ga.. , jha.. ca / vakārodaramadhyasthaṃ ṭhakāreṇeti ṅa.. ,
cha.. ca
:p 75
133.d:
जकारं विन्दुसंयुक्तं ओङ्कारेण समन्वितं /
धकारोदरमध्यस्थं वकारेण निबोधितं(3) //
:न्
1 नागयन्त्रे इति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 रक्षामन्त्रमिति ख.. , ग.. , ङ.. , ज.. च
3 ककारोदरमध्यस्थं चकारेणेति ख.. / चकारोदरमध्यस्थं
चकारेणेति ग.. , झ.. च / वकारोदरमध्यस्थं ठकारेणेति ङ.. ,
छ.. च
:प् 75
133.m:
the syllable "ja" joined with the bindu, accompanied by the syllable "oṃ", / situated in the middle of the belly of the syllable "dha", awakened by the syllable "va",
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "nāgayantre" in MSS gha and ña.
[Variant reading:] "rakṣāmantram" in MSS kha, ga, ṅa, and ja.
[Variant reading:] "kakārodaramadhyasthaṃ cakāreṇa" in MS kha; "cakārodaramadhyasthaṃ cakāreṇa" in MSS ga and jha; "vakārodaramadhyasthaṃ ṭhakāreṇa" in MSS ṅa and cha.

133.s:
candrasampuṭamadhyasthaṃ sarvaduṣṭavimardakam(1) /
athavā karṇikāyāñca likhennāma ca kāraṇam //
133.d:
चन्द्रसम्पुटमध्यस्थं सर्वदुष्टविमर्दकम्(1) /
अथवा कर्णिकायाञ्च लिखेन्नाम च कारणम् //
133.m: situated within the lunar enclosure, crushing all wicked ones. / Or else, one should write the name and the cause in the pericarp.

133.s:
pūrve dale tathoṅkāraṃ svadakṣe cottare likhet /
āgneyyādau ca hūṅkārandale ṣoḍaśake svarān //
133.d:
पूर्वे दले तथोङ्कारं स्वदक्षे चोत्तरे लिखेत् /
आग्नेय्यादौ च हूङ्कारन्दले षोडशके स्वरान् //
133.m: Likewise, one should write the syllable "oṃ" on the eastern petal, on one's right, and on the northern petal; / and the syllable "hūṃ" in the southeast and the other [intermediate directions], and the vowels on the sixteen petals;

133.s:
catustriṃśaddale kādyān vāhye mantrañca mṛtyujit /
likhedvaibhūrjapatre tu rocanākuṅgkumena ca //
133.d:
चतुस्त्रिंशद्दले काद्यान् वाह्ये मन्त्रञ्च मृत्युजित् /
लिखेद्वैभूर्जपत्रे तु रोचनाकुङ्ग्कुमेन च //
133.m: the consonants beginning with "ka" on thirty-four petals, and the Mṛtyujit mantra on the outside. / One should write it indeed on birch bark with yellow pigment and saffron,

133.s:
karpūracandanābhyāñca śvetasūteṇa veṣṭayet /
sikthakena paricchādya kalaśopari pūjayet //
133.d:
कर्पूरचन्दनाभ्याञ्च श्वेतसूतेण वेष्टयेत् /
सिक्थकेन परिच्छाद्य कलशोपरि पूजयेत् //
133.m: and with camphor and sandalwood; one should wrap it with a white thread. / Having covered it with beeswax, one should worship it atop a water-pot.

133.s:
yantrasya(2) dhāraṇādrāgāḥ śāmyanti ripavo mṛtiḥ /
vidyāntu bhelakhīṃ vakṣye viprayogamṛterharīṃ(3) //
oṃ vātale vitale viḍālamukhi indraputri udbhavo vāyudevena khīli ājī
hājā mayi vāha ihādi duḥkhanityakaṇṭhoccair muhūrtānvayā aha
māṃ yasmahaṃ upāḍi oṃ bhelakhi oṃ svāhā
133.d:
यन्त्रस्य(2) धारणाद्रागाः शाम्यन्ति रिपवो मृतिः /
विद्यान्तु भेलखीं वक्ष्ये विप्रयोगमृतेर्हरीं(3) //
ओं वातले वितले विडालमुखि इन्द्रपुत्रि उद्भवो वायुदेवेन खीलि आजी
हाजा मयि वाह इहादि दुःखनित्यकण्ठोच्चैर् मुहूर्तान्वया अह
मां यस्महं उपाडि ओं भेलखि ओं स्वाहा
133.m:
From wearing the yantra, passions, enemies, and death are pacified. / I shall explain the Bhelakhī spell, which removes the separation and death:
"Oṃ, Vātalā, Vitalā, cat-faced one, daughter of Indra, born from the wind-god, khīli ājī / hājā, bear into me! Here and elsewhere, endowed with the moment of the high neck of continuous distress, aha / mām yasmaham upāḍi, oṃ bhelakhi oṃ svāhā!"

133.s:
navadurgāsaptajaptānmukhastambho mukhasthitāt /
oṃ caṇḍi oṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā
gṛhītvā saptajaptaṃ tu khadgayuddhe 'parājitaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave nānābalāni nāma
trayastriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 sarvaduḥkhavimardakamiti jha..
2 mantrasyeti ka.. , kha.. , ga.. , cha.. ca
3 ripurogamṛterharīmiti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. , jha. ña.. ca
:p 76
:ś atha catustriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
trailokyavijayavidyā
133.d:
नवदुर्गासप्तजप्तान्मुखस्तम्भो मुखस्थितात् /
ओं चण्डि ओं हूं फट् स्वाहा
गृहीत्वा सप्तजप्तं तु खद्गयुद्धे ऽपराजितः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे नानाबलानि नाम
त्रयस्त्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 सर्वदुःखविमर्दकमिति झ..
2 मन्त्रस्येति क.. , ख.. , ग.. , छ.. च
3 रिपुरोगमृतेर्हरीमिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. , झ. ञ.. च
:प् 76
:श् अथ चतुस्त्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
त्रैलोक्यविजयविद्या
133.m:
From [the root of] Navadurgā recited seven times, placed in the mouth, paralysis of the mouth [occurs].
"Oṃ Caṇḍi oṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!"
Having taken it, recited over seven times, one is undefeated in sword-combat.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-third chapter, entitled "Various Armies," in the Ocean of Victory in War in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "sarvaduḥkhavimardakam" in MS jha.
[Variant reading:] "mantrasya" in MSS ka, kha, ga, and cha.
[Variant reading:] "ripurogamṛterharīm" in MSS ga, gha, ṅa, ja, jha, and ña.
Now begins the one hundred and thirty-fourth chapter:
The Trailokyavijayā Spell.

134.s:
īśvara uvāca
trailokyavijayāṃ vakṣye sarvayantravimardanīṃ(1) /
oṃ hūṃ kṣūṃ hrūṃ oṃ namo bhagavati daṃṣṭriṇi
bhīmavaktre mahograrūpe hili hili raktanetre kili kili mahānisvane kulu oṃ
vidyujjihve kulu oṃ nirmāṃse kaṭa kaṭa gonasābharaṇe cili cili
śavamālādhāriṇi drāvaya oṃ mahāraudri sārdracarmakṛtācchade(2)
vijṛmbha oṃ nṛtya asilatādhāriṇi bhṛkuṭīkṛtāpāṅge
viṣamanetrakṛtānane vasāmedoviliptagātre kaha 2 oṃ hasa 2 kruddha 2
oṃ nīlajīmūtavarṇe oṃ hrām hrīṃ hrūṃ raudrarūpe hūṃ
hrīṃ klīṃ oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ oṃ ākarṣa oṃ dhūna 2 oṃ he
haḥ khaḥ vajriṇi hūṃ kṣūṃ kṣāṃ krodharūpiṇi prajvala 2
oṃ bhīmabhīṣaṇe bhinda oṃ mahākāye cchinda oṃ karālini kiṭi
2 mahābhūtamātaḥ sarvaduṣṭanivāriṇi jaye oṃ vijaye oṃ
trailokyavijaye hūṃ phaṭ svāhā
:n
1 sarvamantravimardanīmiti kha..
134.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
त्रैलोक्यविजयां वक्ष्ये सर्वयन्त्रविमर्दनीं(1) /
ओं हूं क्षूं ह्रूं ओं नमो भगवति दंष्ट्रिणि
भीमवक्त्रे महोग्ररूपे हिलि हिलि रक्तनेत्रे किलि किलि महानिस्वने कुलु ओं
विद्युज्जिह्वे कुलु ओं निर्मांसे कट कट गोनसाभरणे चिलि चिलि
शवमालाधारिणि द्रावय ओं महारौद्रि सार्द्रचर्मकृताच्छदे(2)
विजृम्भ ओं नृत्य असिलताधारिणि भृकुटीकृतापाङ्गे
विषमनेत्रकृतानने वसामेदोविलिप्तगात्रे कह 2 ओं हस 2 क्रुद्ध 2
ओं नीलजीमूतवर्णे ओं ह्राम् ह्रीं ह्रूं रौद्ररूपे हूं
ह्रीं क्लीं ओं ह्रीं हूं ओं आकर्ष ओं धून 2 ओं हे
हः खः वज्रिणि हूं क्षूं क्षां क्रोधरूपिणि प्रज्वल 2
ओं भीमभीषणे भिन्द ओं महाकाये च्छिन्द ओं करालिनि किटि
2 महाभूतमातः सर्वदुष्टनिवारिणि जये ओं विजये ओं
त्रैलोक्यविजये हूं फट् स्वाहा
:न्
1 सर्वमन्त्रविमर्दनीमिति ख..
134.m:
The Lord said: / I shall declare Trailokyavijayā, which destroys all yantras:
"Oṃ hūṃ kṣūṃ hrūṃ oṃ, obeisance to the goddess! Fang-bearing one, / terrible-faced one, of immensely fierce form, hili hili! Red-eyed one, kili kili! Loud-sounding one, kulu oṃ! / Lightning-tongued one, kulu oṃ! Fleshless one, kaṭa kaṭa! Adorned with venomous vipers, cili cili! / Wearer of a garland of corpses, cause them to flee! Oṃ, greatly fierce one, covered with fresh, wet skin, / yawn! Oṃ, dance, bearer of the sword-creeper, with knitted brows and curved side-glances, / having a face distorted by uneven eyes, whose body is smeared with fat and marrow! Kaha kaha, oṃ, laugh, laugh! Enraged one, / of the dark colour of a raincloud! Oṃ hrām hrīṃ hrūṃ, fierce-formed one, hūṃ / hrīṃ klīṃ oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ oṃ, attract! Oṃ, shake, shake! Oṃ he / haḥ khaḥ, thunderbolt-bearer, hūṃ kṣūṃ kṣāṃ, wrathful-formed one, blaze, blaze! / Oṃ, frightfully terrifying one, pierce! Oṃ, gigantic-bodied one, cleave! Oṃ, dreadful one, kiṭi / kiṭi, mother of the great spirits, dispeller of all evil ones, Jaya, oṃ Vijaya, oṃ / Trailokyavijaya, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!"
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "sarvamantravimardanīm" in MS kha.

134.s:
2 sārdracarmakṛtāmbare iti jha..
:p 77
nīlavarṇāṃ pretasaṃsthāṃ viṃśahastāṃ yajejjaye //
134.d:
2 सार्द्रचर्मकृताम्बरे इति झ..
:प् 77
नीलवर्णां प्रेतसंस्थां विंशहस्तां यजेज्जये //
134.m:
[Variant reading:] "sārdracarmakṛtāmbare" in MS jha.
For victory, one should worship the dark-complexioned, twenty-armed [goddess] standing upon a corpse.

134.s:
nyāsaṃ kṛtvā tu pañcāṅgaṃ raktapuṣpāṇi homayet /
saṅgrāme sainyabhaṅgaḥ syāt trailokyatrijayāpāṭhāt //
134.d:
न्यासं कृत्वा तु पञ्चाङ्गं रक्तपुष्पाणि होमयेत् /
सङ्ग्रामे सैन्यभङ्गः स्यात् त्रैलोक्यत्रिजयापाठात् //
134.m: Having performed the five-limbed nyāsa, one should offer red flowers into the fire. / In battle, the routing of an army will occur from the recitation of the Trailokyavijayā.

134.s:
oṃ bahurūpāya stambhaya stambhaya oṃ mohaya oṃ sarvaśatrūn
drāvaya oṃ brahmāṇamākarṣaya viṣṇumākarṣaya oṃ
māheśvaramākarṣaya oṃ indraṃ ṭālaya oṃ parvatān cālaya oṃ
saptasāgarān śoṣaya oṃ chinda chinda bahurūpāya namaḥ
bhujaṅgannāmamṛnmūrtisaṃsthaṃ vidyādarintataḥ
//3//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave trailokyavijayavidyā nāma
caturtriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
saṅgrāmavijayavidyā
134.d:
ओं बहुरूपाय स्तम्भय स्तम्भय ओं मोहय ओं सर्वशत्रून्
द्रावय ओं ब्रह्माणमाकर्षय विष्णुमाकर्षय ओं
माहेश्वरमाकर्षय ओं इन्द्रं टालय ओं पर्वतान् चालय ओं
सप्तसागरान् शोषय ओं छिन्द छिन्द बहुरूपाय नमः
भुजङ्गन्नाममृन्मूर्तिसंस्थं विद्यादरिन्ततः
//3//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे त्रैलोक्यविजयविद्या नाम
चतुर्त्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
सङ्ग्रामविजयविद्या
134.m:
"Oṃ, to Bahurūpa, paralyze, paralyze! Oṃ, delude! Oṃ, cause all enemies / to flee! Oṃ, attract Brahmā! Attract Viṣṇu! Oṃ, / attract Māheśvara! Oṃ, shake Indra! Oṃ, move the mountains! Oṃ, / dry up the seven oceans! Oṃ, cleave, cleave, obeisance to Bahurūpa!" / Then the spell-adept [places] a serpent abiding in a clay image bearing the name. //3
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Trailokyavijayā Spell," in the Ocean of Victory in War in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the one hundred and thirty-fifth chapter:
The Saṅgrāmavijayā Spell.

135.s:
īśvara uvāca
saṅgrāmavijayāṃ vidyāṃ padamālāṃ vadāmyahaṃ /
oṃ hrīṃ cāmuṇḍe śmaśānavāsini khaṭvāṅgakapālahaste(1)
:n
1 khaḍgakapālahaste iti jha..
:p 78
135.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
सङ्ग्रामविजयां विद्यां पदमालां वदाम्यहं /
ओं ह्रीं चामुण्डे श्मशानवासिनि खट्वाङ्गकपालहस्ते(1)
:न्
1 खड्गकपालहस्ते इति झ..
:प् 78
135.m:
The Lord said: / I shall state the Saṅgrāmavijayā spell, an unbroken series of words:
"Oṃ hrīṃ Cāmuṇḍā, dweller in the cremation ground, holding a skull-topped staff and a skull cup in hand—"
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "khaḍgakapālahaste" in MS jha.

135.s:
mahapretasamārūḍhe mahāvimānasamākule kālarātri
mahāgaṇaparivṛte mahāmukhe bahubhuje
ghaṇṭāḍamarukiṅkaṇīaṭṭāṭṭahāse kili kili oṃ hūṃ
phaṭ daṃṣṭrāghorāndhakāriṇi nādaśabdabahule
gajacarmaprāvṛtaśarīre māṃsadigdhe lelihānograjihve mahārākṣasi
raudradaṃṣṭrākarāle bhaumāṭṭāṭṭahāse sphuradvidyutprabhe
cala cala oṃ cakoranetre cili cili oṃ lalajjihve oṃ bhīṃ bhrukuṭīmukhi
huṅkārabhayatrāsanikapālamālāveṣṭitajaṭāmukuṭaśaśāṅkadhāriṇi aṭṭāṭṭahāse kili kili oṃ hrūṃ
daṃṣṭrāghorāndhakāriṇi sarvavighnavināśini idaṃ karma sādhaya
2 oṃ śīghraṃ kuru 2 oṃ phaṭ oṃ aṅkuśena śamaya praveśaya
oṃ raṅga raṅga kampaya 2 oṃ cālaya oṃ rudhiramāṃsamadyapriye
hana 2 oṃ kuṭṭa 2 oṃ chinda oṃ māraya oṃ anukramaya oṃ
vajraśarīrampātaya(1) oṃ trailokyagatanduṣṭamaduṣṭaṃ vā
gṛhītamagṛhītaṃ vā āveśaya oṃ nṛtya oṃ vanda oṃ
koṭarākṣi ūrdhvakeśi ulūkavadane karaṅkiṇi oṃ
karaṅkamālādhāriṇi daha oṃ paca 2 oṃ gṛhṇa oṃ
maṇḍalamadhye praveśaya oṃ kiṃ vilambasi brahmasatyena
viṣṇusatyena rudrasatyena ṛṣisatyena āveśaya oṃ kili kili oṃ khili
khili vili vili oṃ vikṛtarūpadhāriṇi
kṛṣṇabhujaṅgaveṣṭitaśarīre sarvagrahāveśani
pralambauṣṭhini bhrūbhaṅgalagnanāsike vikaṭamukhi kapilajaṭe
brāhmibhañja(2) oṃ jvalāmukhi(3)
135.d:
महप्रेतसमारूढे महाविमानसमाकुले कालरात्रि
महागणपरिवृते महामुखे बहुभुजे

135.m: "O you who mount a great corpse, who are surrounded by great aerial chariots, Kālarātri, surrounded by great retinues, huge-faced one, many-armed one! O you who roar with loud laughter amidst the sound of bells, ḍamaru-drums, and tinkling ornaments, kili kili, oṃ hūṃ phaṭ! O you who cause dreadful darkness with your fangs, who abound in sounds and clamour, whose body is wrapped in elephant skin, smeared with flesh, with your fierce licking tongue, great demoness! Terrifying with dreadful fangs, bursting with earth-shaking loud laughter, glowing like flashing lightning! Move, move, oṃ! O bird-eyed one, cili cili, oṃ! O flickering-tongued one, oṃ bhīṃ! O frowning-faced one, terrifying with fearful huṅkāras, wearing the moon on your matted-hair crown surrounded by a garland of skulls, laughing uproariously, kili kili, oṃ hrūṃ! O creator of terrifying darkness with your fangs, destroyer of all obstacles, accomplish this rite, accomplish! Oṃ, make haste, make haste! Oṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, subdue with the elephant goad, make [them] enter! Oṃ raṅga raṅga, make [them] tremble, make [them] tremble! Oṃ, shake! Oṃ, you who delight in blood, flesh, and liquor! Strike, strike! Oṃ, crush, crush! Oṃ, cut, oṃ, slay, oṃ, make [them] submit, oṃ, cast down their adamantine body! Oṃ, whether evil or not evil residing in the three worlds, whether seized or not seized, possess [them]! Oṃ, dance! Oṃ, bow! Oṃ, hollow-eyed one, upright-haired one, owl-faced one, skeletal one, oṃ! O wearer of a garland of skeletons, burn, oṃ, cook, cook, oṃ, seize, oṃ! Make [them] enter the center of the maṇḍala! Oṃ, why do you delay? By the truth of Brahmā, by the truth of Viṣṇu, by the truth of Rudra, by the truth of the sages, possess [them]! Oṃ kili kili, oṃ khili khili vili vili, oṃ! O bearer of a deformed shape, whose body is entwined with black serpents, possessor of all astrological spirits! O hanging-lipped one, whose nose reaches the furrow of your brows, hideous-faced one, yellow-matted-haired one, Brāhmī, shatter! Oṃ flame-faced one!"

135.m: "Dig, oṃ! Cast down, oṃ! Red-eyed one, whirl around, throw to the ground! Oṃ, seize the head, shut the eyes! Oṃ, seize the hands and feet, break the seal! Oṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, tear apart, oṃ! Cut with the trident, oṃ! Strike with the vajra, oṃ! Beat with the staff, beat! Oṃ, slice with the discus, slice! Oṃ, pierce with the spear! Pierce with the fangs, oṃ! Cleave with the lotus-seed, oṃ! Seize with the elephant goad, oṃ! Release, release the fevers of head and eyes—the quotidian, tertian, quartan, [and so forth]—and the spirits of Ḍākinīs and Skanda! Oṃ, cook, oṃ, ruin, oṃ, throw to the ground, oṃ, seize! Oṃ, Brahmāṇī, come! Oṃ, Māheśvarī, come! Oṃ, Kaumārī, come! Oṃ, Vaiṣṇavī, come! Oṃ, Vārāhī, come! Oṃ, Aindrī, come! Oṃ, Cāmuṇḍā, come! Oṃ, Revatī, come! Oṃ, Sky-Revatī, come! Oṃ, rover on the Himavat, come! Destroyer of Ruru, destroyer of asuras, sky-traveler! Bind with the noose, bind! Subdue with the elephant goad, subdue! Stand by the agreement! Oṃ, make [them] enter the maṇḍala! Oṃ, seize, bind the mouth! Oṃ, bind the eyes, and bind the hands and feet! Bind all the malicious spirits! Oṃ, bind the cardinal directions, oṃ, bind the intermediate directions, bind the lower regions! Oṃ, bind everything! Oṃ, through ashes, water, earth, or mustard seeds, possess all of them! Oṃ, strike down, oṃ! Cāmuṇḍā, kili kili, oṃ vicce huṃ phaṭ svāhā!"
This garland of words is called Jayā ('Victorious'); it accomplishes all rites.

Auspiciousness or inauspiciousness is to be known from the planet occupying the trio of channels. / That diagram of the Lord of Serpents is adorned with three channels.

136.m:
Situated under the Sun, Mars, Saturn, or Rāhu, it would be inauspicious; otherwise, it is auspicious. / When associated with region and village, brothers, wife, and so forth, individually they are auspicious.
A, Bha, Kṛ, Ro, Mṛ, Ā, Pu, Pu, Ā, Ma, Pū, U, Ha, Ci, Svā, Vi, A, Jye, Mū, Pū, U, A, Dha, Śa, Pū, U, Re: here twenty-seven lunar mansions are to be known.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, in the section on the ocean of victory in war, the one hundred and thirty-sixth chapter, entitled 'The Lunar Mansion Diagram'.
Now, the one hundred and thirty-seventh chapter.
The Lore of Mahāmārī

137.s:
īśvara uvāca
mahāmārīṃ pravakṣyāmi vidyāṃ śatruvimardinīṃ /
:n
1 cakramphaṇīśvarantadvat iti ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , jha.. , ña.. ca
:p 82
oṃ hrīṃ mahāmāri raktākṣi kṛṣṇavarṇe
yamasyājñākariṇi sarvabhūtasaṃhārakāriṇi amukaṃ hana 2 oṃ daha
2 paca 2 oṃ chinda 2 oṃ māraya 2 oṃ utsādaya 2 oṃ
sarvasattvavaśaṅkari sarvakāmike huṃ phaṭ svāheti
oṃ māri hṛdayāya namaḥ / oṃ mahāmāri śirase svāhā / oṃ
kālarātri śikhāyai vauṣaṭ / oṃ kṛṣṇavarṇe khaḥ kavacāya
huṃ / oṃ tārakākṣi vidyujjihve sarvasattvabhayaṅkari rakṣa 2
sarvakāryeṣu hraṃ trinetrāya caṣaṭ / oṃ mahāmāri
sarvabhūtadamāni mahākāli astrāya huṃ phaṭ
eṣa nyāsī mahādevi kartavyaḥ sādhakena tu //
137.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
महामारीं प्रवक्ष्यामि विद्यां शत्रुविमर्दिनीं /
:न्
1 चक्रम्फणीश्वरन्तद्वत् इति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , झ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 82
ओं ह्रीं महामारि रक्ताक्षि कृष्णवर्णे
यमस्याज्ञाकरिणि सर्वभूतसंहारकारिणि अमुकं हन 2 ओं दह
2 पच 2 ओं छिन्द 2 ओं मारय 2 ओं उत्सादय 2 ओं
सर्वसत्त्ववशङ्करि सर्वकामिके हुं फट् स्वाहेति
ओं मारि हृदयाय नमः / ओं महामारि शिरसे स्वाहा / ओं
कालरात्रि शिखायै वौषट् / ओं कृष्णवर्णे खः कवचाय
हुं / ओं तारकाक्षि विद्युज्जिह्वे सर्वसत्त्वभयङ्करि रक्ष 2
सर्वकार्येषु ह्रं त्रिनेत्राय चषट् / ओं महामारि
सर्वभूतदमानि महाकालि अस्त्राय हुं फट्
एष न्यासी महादेवि कर्तव्यः साधकेन तु //
137.m:
The Lord said: / I shall declare Mahāmārī, the spell that crushes enemies:
[Footnote]
1 'cakramphaṇīśvarantadvat' in manuscripts ga.., gha.., ṅa.., jha.., and ña..
"Oṃ hrīṃ, Mahāmārī, red-eyed one, black-colored one, obedient to the command of Yama, bringer of destruction to all beings! Strike such-and-such, strike! Oṃ, burn, burn, cook, cook! Oṃ, cut, cut! Oṃ, kill, kill! Oṃ, ruin, ruin! Oṃ, you who subjugate all living beings, who grant all desires, huṃ phaṭ svāhā!"
“Oṃ, homage to the heart of Māri! Oṃ, svāhā to the head of Mahāmāri! Oṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest of Kālarātri! Oṃ, khaḥ huṃ to the armor of the Dark-colored One!
Oṃ, O Star-eyed One, Lightning-tongued One, Terrifier of all beings, protect, protect in all endeavors, hraṃ caṣaṭ to the three-eyed one! Oṃ, Mahāmāri, Subduer of all beings, Mahākālī, huṃ phaṭ to the weapon!”
This ritual deposition, O Great Goddess, should indeed be performed by the practitioner.

137.s:
śavādivastramādāya caturasrantrihastakaṃ /
kṛṣṇavarṇāṃ trivaktrāñca caturbāhuṃ samālikhet //
137.d:
शवादिवस्त्रमादाय चतुरस्रन्त्रिहस्तकं /
कृष्णवर्णां त्रिवक्त्राञ्च चतुर्बाहुं समालिखेत् //
137.m: Taking a cloth [from a corpse] or the like, square [and] three cubits in size, / one should paint [her] dark-colored, three-faced, and four-armed,

137.s:
paṭe vicitravarṇaiś ca dhanuḥ śūlañca kartṛkāṃ(1) /
khaṭvāṅgandhārayantīṃ ca kṛṣṇābhaṃ pūrvamānanaṃ //
137.d:
पटे विचित्रवर्णैश् च धनुः शूलञ्च कर्तृकां(1) /
खट्वाङ्गन्धारयन्तीं च कृष्णाभं पूर्वमाननं //
137.m: on the cloth with various colors, bearing a bow, a trident, a curved knife, / and a skull-staff, her eastern face dark-hued.

137.s:
tasya dṛṣṭinipātena bhakṣayedagrato naraṃ /
dvitīyaṃ yāmyabhāge tu raktajihvaṃ bhayānakaṃ //
137.d:
तस्य दृष्टिनिपातेन भक्षयेदग्रतो नरं /
द्वितीयं याम्यभागे तु रक्तजिह्वं भयानकं //
137.m: By the falling of its glance, it devours the man in front. / The second face, on the southern side, is red-tongued and terrifying,

137.s:
lelihānaṃ karālaṃ ca daṃṣṭrotkaṭabhayānakaṃ /
tasya dṛṣṭinipātena bhakṣyamāṇaṃ hayādikaṃ //
137.d:
लेलिहानं करालं च दंष्ट्रोत्कटभयानकं /
तस्य दृष्टिनिपातेन भक्ष्यमाणं हयादिकं //
137.m: licking, dreadful, and fierce with prominent fangs; / by the falling of its glance, horses and the like are devoured.

137.s:
tṛtīyaṃ ca sukhaṃ devyāḥ śvetavarṇaṃ gajādinut /
gandhapuṣpādimadhvājyaiḥ paścimābhimukhaṃ yajet //
:n
1 sadhanuḥśūlakartṛkāmiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 83
137.d:
तृतीयं च सुखं देव्याः श्वेतवर्णं गजादिनुत् /
गन्धपुष्पादिमध्वाज्यैः पश्चिमाभिमुखं यजेत् //
:न्
1 सधनुःशूलकर्तृकामिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 83
137.m:
And the third face of the goddess is pleasant, white-colored, repelling elephants and the like; / facing westward, one should worship [it] with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, honey, and clarified butter.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] “sadhanuḥśūlakartṛkām” according to manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, ja, and ña.

137.s:
mantrasmṛterakṣirogaśirorogādi naśyati /
vaśyāḥ syuryakṣarakṣāś ca nāśamāyānti śatravaḥ //
137.d:
मन्त्रस्मृतेरक्षिरोगशिरोरोगादि नश्यति /
वश्याः स्युर्यक्षरक्षाश् च नाशमायान्ति शत्रवः //
137.m: From the recollection of the mantra, eye diseases, head diseases, and the like are destroyed; / yakṣas and rākṣasas become subdued, and enemies meet destruction.

137.s:
samidho nimbavṛkṣasya hy ajāraktavimiśritāḥ /
mārayet krodhasaṃyukto homādeva na saṃśayaḥ //
137.d:
समिधो निम्बवृक्षस्य ह्य् अजारक्तविमिश्रिताः /
मारयेत् क्रोधसंयुक्तो होमादेव न संशयः //
137.m: Filled with anger, [the practitioner] would certainly kill [an enemy] / by a fire oblation of firewood of the neem tree mixed with goat's blood; of this there is no doubt.

137.s:
parasainyamukho bhūtvā saptāhaṃ juhuyādyadi /
vyādhibhirgṛhyate sainyambhaṅgo bhavati vairiṇaḥ //
137.d:
परसैन्यमुखो भूत्वा सप्ताहं जुहुयाद्यदि /
व्याधिभिर्गृह्यते सैन्यम्भङ्गो भवति वैरिणः //
137.m: If he offers oblations for seven days facing the enemy army, / the army is seized with diseases, and the enemy suffers defeat.

137.s:
samidho 'ṣṭasahasrantu yasya nāmnā tu homayet /
acirān mriyate sopi brahmaṇā yadi rakṣitaḥ //
137.d:
समिधो ऽष्टसहस्रन्तु यस्य नाम्ना तु होमयेत् /
अचिरान् म्रियते सोपि ब्रह्मणा यदि रक्षितः //
137.m: He in whose name one offers eight thousand sticks of kindling / dies without delay, even if protected by Brahmā.

137.s:
unmattasamidho raktaviṣayuktasahasrakaṃ /
dinatrayaṃ sasainyaś ca nāśamāyāti vai ripuḥ //
137.d:
उन्मत्तसमिधो रक्तविषयुक्तसहस्रकं /
दिनत्रयं ससैन्यश् च नाशमायाति वै रिपुः //
137.m: For three days, with a thousand kindling sticks of datura mixed with blood and poison, / the enemy indeed meets destruction along with his army.

137.d:
राजिकालवर्णैर् होमाद्भङ्गो ऽरेः स्याद् दिनत्रयात् /
खररक्तसमायुक्तहोमादुच्चाटयेद्रिपुं //
137.m: By a fire oblation with black mustard seeds and salt, the defeat of the enemy occurs within three days; / by an oblation combined with donkey’s blood, he expels the enemy.

137.s:
kākaraktasamāyogāddhomādutsādanaṃ hy areḥ /
badhāya kurute sarvaṃ yat kiñcinmanasepsitaṃ //
137.d:
काकरक्तसमायोगाद्धोमादुत्सादनं ह्य् अरेः /
बधाय कुरुते सर्वं यत् किञ्चिन्मनसेप्सितं //
137.m: By an oblation combined with crow's blood, the eradication of the enemy is effected; / he accomplishes whatever his mind desires for [the enemy's] slaying.

137.s:
atha saṅgrāmasamaye gajārūḍhastu sādhakaḥ /
kumārīdvayasaṃyukto mantrasannaddhavigrahaḥ //
137.d:
अथ सङ्ग्रामसमये गजारूढस्तु साधकः /
कुमारीद्वयसंयुक्तो मन्त्रसन्नद्धविग्रहः //
137.m: Now, at the time of battle, the practitioner, mounted upon an elephant, / accompanied by two virgins, his body equipped with mantras,

137.s:
dūraśaṅkhādivādyani vidyayā hy ābhimantrayet /
mahāmāyāpaṭaṃ gṛhya ucchettavyaṃ raṇājire //
137.d:
दूरशङ्खादिवाद्यनि विद्यया ह्य् आभिमन्त्रयेत् /
महामायापटं गृह्य उच्छेत्तव्यं रणाजिरे //
137.m: should consecrate conches and musical instruments from afar with the mantra-science; / holding the Mahāmāyā cloth, he should cut down [the foes] on the battlefield.

137.s:
parasainyamukho bhūtvā darśayettaṃ mahāpaṭaṃ /
kumārīrbhojayettatra paścātpiṇḍīñca bhrāmayet //
137.d:
परसैन्यमुखो भूत्वा दर्शयेत्तं महापटं /
कुमारीर्भोजयेत्तत्र पश्चात्पिण्डीञ्च भ्रामयेत् //
137.m: Facing the enemy army, he should display that great cloth; / he should feed the virgins there, and afterwards rotate the ritual ball of food.

137.s:
sādhakaścintayetsainyampāṣāṇamiva niś calaṃ /
nirutsāhaṃ vibhagnañca muhyamānañca bhāvayet //
137.d:
साधकश्चिन्तयेत्सैन्यम्पाषाणमिव निश् चलं /
निरुत्साहं विभग्नञ्च मुह्यमानञ्च भावयेत् //
137.m: The practitioner should visualize the army as motionless like a rock; / he should visualize it as devoid of enthusiasm, routed, and bewildered.

137.s:
eṣa stambho mayā prokto na deyo yasya kasya cit /
:p 84
trailokyavijayā māyā durgaivaṃ bhairavī tathā //
137.d:
एष स्तम्भो मया प्रोक्तो न देयो यस्य कस्य चित् /
:प् 84
त्रैलोक्यविजया माया दुर्गैवं भैरवी तथा //
137.m:
This immobilization has been taught by me; it should not be given to just anyone.
[Page] 84
Trailokyavijayā, Māyā, Durgā likewise, Bhairavī,

137.s:
kubjikā bhairavo rudro nārasiṃhapaṭādinā //19//
:e ity āgneye mahāopurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave mahāmārī nāma
saptatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṣaṭkarmāṇi
137.d:
कुब्जिका भैरवो रुद्रो नारसिंहपटादिना //19//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महाओपुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे महामारी नाम
सप्तत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
षट्कर्माणि
137.m:
Kubjikā, Bhairava, Rudra, through the cloth of Nṛsiṃha and so forth. //19
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, in the Ocean of Victory in Battle, the one hundred thirty-seventh chapter, entitled “Mahāmārī.”
Now the one hundred thirty-eighth chapter.
The Six Ritual Acts

138.s:
īśvara uvāca
ṣaṭkarmāṇi pravakṣyāmi sarvamantreṣu tacchṛṇu /
ādau sādhyaṃ likhet pūrvaṃ cānte mantrasamanvitaṃ //
138.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
षट्कर्माणि प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वमन्त्रेषु तच्छृणु /
आदौ साध्यं लिखेत् पूर्वं चान्ते मन्त्रसमन्वितं //
138.m: The Lord said: / I shall declare the six ritual acts in all mantras; listen to that! / At the beginning one should first write the name of the target, and at the end endowed with the mantra:

138.s:
pallavaḥ sa tu vijñeyo mahoccāṭakaraḥ paraḥ /
ādau mantraḥ tataḥ sādhyo madhye sādhyaḥ punarmanuḥ //
138.d:
पल्लवः स तु विज्ञेयो महोच्चाटकरः परः /
आदौ मन्त्रः ततः साध्यो मध्ये साध्यः पुनर्मनुः //
138.m: that is known as the pallava, supreme in effecting great expulsion. / At the beginning is the mantra, then the target; in the middle is the target, then the mantra again:

138.s:
yogākhyaḥ sampradāyo 'yaṅkulotsādeṣu yojayet /
ādau mantrapadandadyānmadhye sādhyaṃ niyojayet //
138.d:
योगाख्यः सम्प्रदायो ऽयङ्कुलोत्सादेषु योजयेत् /
आदौ मन्त्रपदन्दद्यान्मध्ये साध्यं नियोजयेत् //
138.m: this method is named yoga; one should employ it in the eradication of families. / One should place the mantra-phrase at the beginning, and insert the target in the middle;

138.s:
punaścānte likhenmantraṃ sādhyaṃ mantrapadaṃ punaḥ /
:p 85
rodhakaḥ sampradāyastu stambhanādiṣu yojayet //
138.d:
पुनश्चान्ते लिखेन्मन्त्रं साध्यं मन्त्रपदं पुनः /
:प् 85
रोधकः सम्प्रदायस्तु स्तम्भनादिषु योजयेत् //
138.m:
and at the end one should again write the mantra, the target, and then the mantra-phrase:
[Page] 85
this method is rodhaka; one should employ it in rituals of immobilization and the like.

138.s:
adhordhvaṃ yāmyavāme tu(1) madhye sādhyantu yojayet /
sampuṭaḥ satu vijñeyo vaśyākarṣeṣu yojayet //
138.d:
अधोर्ध्वं याम्यवामे तु(1) मध्ये साध्यन्तु योजयेत् /
सम्पुटः सतु विज्ञेयो वश्याकर्षेषु योजयेत् //
138.m: Below, above, to the right, and to the left, and one should place the target in the center; / that is known as sampuṭa; one should employ it in rituals of subjugation and attraction.

138.s:
mantrākṣaraṃ yadā sādhyaṃ prathitañcākṣarākṣaraṃ /
prathamaḥ sampradāyaḥ syādākṛṣṭivaśakārakaḥ //
138.d:
मन्त्राक्षरं यदा साध्यं प्रथितञ्चाक्षराक्षरं /
प्रथमः सम्प्रदायः स्यादाकृष्टिवशकारकः //
138.m: When a target and a mantra syllable are interlinked syllable by syllable, / that is the first method, effecting attraction and subjugation.

138.s:
mantrākṣaradvayaṃ likhya ekaṃ sādhyakṣaraṃ punaḥ /
vidarbhaḥ satu vijñeyo vaśyākākarṣeṣu yojayet //
138.d:
मन्त्राक्षरद्वयं लिख्य एकं साध्यक्षरं पुनः /
विदर्भः सतु विज्ञेयो वश्याकाकर्षेषु योजयेत् //
138.m: Having written two mantra syllables, then one syllable of the target: / that is known as vidarbha; one should employ it in rituals of subjugation and attraction.

138.s:
ākarṣaṇād yat karma vasante caiva kārayet /
tāpajvare tathā vaśye svāhā cākarṣaṇe śubhaṃ //
138.d:
आकर्षणाद् यत् कर्म वसन्ते चैव कारयेत् /
तापज्वरे तथा वश्ये स्वाहा चाकर्षणे शुभं //
138.m: The rite of attraction and the like should indeed be performed in the spring season. / In burning fever, likewise in subjugation, and in attraction, “svāhā” is auspicious.

138.s:
namaskārapadañcaiva śāntivṛddhau prayojayet /
pauṣṭikeṣu vaṣaṭkāramākarṣe vaśakarmaṇi //
138.d:
नमस्कारपदञ्चैव शान्तिवृद्धौ प्रयोजयेत् /
पौष्टिकेषु वषट्कारमाकर्षे वशकर्मणि //
138.m: And one should employ the word of homage (“namaḥ”) in rites of pacification and growth; / the utterance “vaṣaṭ” in nourishing rites, in attraction, and in acts of subjugation;

138.s:
vidveṣoccāṭane mṛtyau phaṭ syāt khaṇḍīkṛtau śubhe /
lābhādau mantradīkṣādau vaṣaṭkārastu siddhidaḥ //
138.d:
विद्वेषोच्चाटने मृत्यौ फट् स्यात् खण्डीकृतौ शुभे /
लाभादौ मन्त्रदीक्षादौ वषट्कारस्तु सिद्धिदः //
138.m: “phaṭ” is for dissension, expulsion, death, and in auspicious cutting. / In attainment and the like, in mantra initiation and the like, the utterance “vaṣaṭ” grants success.

138.s:
yamo 'si yamārājo 'si kālarūpo 'si dharmarāṭ /
mayādattamimaṃ śatrumacireṇa nipātaya //
138.d:
यमो ऽसि यमाराजो ऽसि कालरूपो ऽसि धर्मराट् /
मयादत्तमिमं शत्रुमचिरेण निपातय //
138.m: “You are Yama; you are Yamarāja; you are the embodiment of Time; you are Dharmarāṭ! / Strike down without delay this enemy given by me!”

138.s:
nipātayāmi yatnena nivṛtto bhava sādhaka /
saṃhṛṣṭamanasā(2) brūyāddeśiko 'riprasūdanaḥ //
138.d:
निपातयामि यत्नेन निवृत्तो भव साधक /
संहृष्टमनसा(2) ब्रूयाद्देशिको ऽरिप्रसूदनः //
138.m: “I will strike him down with effort; be at ease, O practitioner!” / With a delighted mind, the spiritual guide, the destroyer of enemies, should speak [thus].

138.s:
padme śukle yamaṃ prārcya homādetat prasiddhyati /
ātmānambhairavaṃ dhyātvā tato madhye kuleśvarīṃ //
138.d:
पद्मे शुक्ले यमं प्रार्च्य होमादेतत् प्रसिद्ध्यति /
आत्मानम्भैरवं ध्यात्वा ततो मध्ये कुलेश्वरीं //
138.m: Having worshipped Yama on a white lotus, this succeeds through fire oblation. / Having meditated on oneself as Bhairava, and then on Kuleśvarī in the center,

138.s:
rātrau vārtāṃ vijānāti ātmanaś ca parasya ca /
:n
1 adha ūrdhvaṃ yāmyavāme iti kha..
2 saṃrambhamanseti cha..
:p 86
durge durge rakṣaṇīti durgāṃ prārcyārihā bhavet //
138.d:
रात्रौ वार्तां विजानाति आत्मनश् च परस्य च /
:न्
1 अध ऊर्ध्वं याम्यवामे इति ख..
2 संरम्भमन्सेति छ..
:प् 86
दुर्गे दुर्गे रक्षणीति दुर्गां प्रार्च्यारिहा भवेत् //
138.m:
at night he knows news of himself and of others.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] “adha ūrdhvaṃ yāmyavāme” according to manuscript kha.
[Variant reading:] “saṃrambhamanasa iti” according to manuscript cha.
Having worshipped Durgā with “Durge, Durge, O Protectress,” he becomes a slayer of enemies.

138.s:
japtvā hasakṣamalavarayumbhairavīṃ ghātayedariṃ //15//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave ṣaṭkarmāṇi
nāmāṣṭatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṣaṣṭisaṃvatsarāḥ
138.d:
जप्त्वा हसक्षमलवरयुम्भैरवीं घातयेदरिं //15//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे षट्कर्माणि
नामाष्टत्रिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
षष्टिसंवत्सराः
138.m:
Having recited [the mantra of] Bhairavī, “hasakṣamalavarayūm,” he slays the enemy. //15
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, in the Ocean of Victory in Battle, the one hundred thirty-eighth chapter, entitled “The Six Ritual Acts.”
Now the one hundred thirty-ninth chapter.
The Sixty Years

139.s:
īśvara uvāca
ṣaṣṭyabdānāṃ pravakṣyāmi śubhāśubhamataḥ śṛṇu /
prabhave yajñakarmāṇi vibhave sukhino janāḥ //
139.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
षष्ट्यब्दानां प्रवक्ष्यामि शुभाशुभमतः शृणु /
प्रभवे यज्ञकर्माणि विभवे सुखिनो जनाः //
139.m: The Lord said: / I will declare the auspicious and inauspicious [effects] of the sixty years; listen to that! / In Prabhava, sacrificial rites [flourish]; in Vibhava, people are happy.

139.s:
śukle ca sarvaśasyāni pramodena pramoditāḥ /
prajāpatau pravṛddhiḥ syādaṅgirā bhogavardhanaḥ //
139.d:
शुक्ले च सर्वशस्यानि प्रमोदेन प्रमोदिताः /
प्रजापतौ प्रवृद्धिः स्यादङ्गिरा भोगवर्धनः //
139.m: And in Śukla, all crops [prosper, and] people are delighted with joy; / in Prajāpati, there is growth; Aṅgiras increases enjoyment.

139.s:
śrīmukhe vardhate loko bhāve bhāvaḥ pravardhate /
pūraṇo pūrate śakro dhātā sarvauṣadhīkaraḥ //
139.d:
श्रीमुखे वर्धते लोको भावे भावः प्रवर्धते /
पूरणो पूरते शक्रो धाता सर्वौषधीकरः //
139.m: In Śrīmukha, the world prospers; in Bhāva, affection increases; / in Yuvan, Indra fills [the earth with rain]; Dhātṛ produces all medicinal plants.

139.s:
īśvaraḥ kṣema ārogyabahudhānyasubhikṣadaḥ /
pramāthī madhyavarṣastu vikrame śasyasampadaḥ //
139.d:
ईश्वरः क्षेम आरोग्यबहुधान्यसुभिक्षदः /
प्रमाथी मध्यवर्षस्तु विक्रमे शस्यसम्पदः //
139.m: Īśvara gives welfare, health, abundant grain, and plentiful food; / Pramāthin has moderate rain, while in Vikrama there is abundance of crops.

139.s:
vṛṣo vṛṣyati sarvāṃś ca citrabhānuś ca citratāṃ /
:p 87
svarbhānuḥ kṣemamārogyaṃ tāraṇe jaladāḥ śubhāḥ //
139.d:
वृषो वृष्यति सर्वांश् च चित्रभानुश् च चित्रतां /
:प् 87
स्वर्भानुः क्षेममारोग्यं तारणे जलदाः शुभाः //
139.m:
Vṛṣa rains upon all, and Citrabhānu brings diversity.
[Page] 87
In Svarbhānu, there is welfare and health; in Tāraṇa, the clouds are auspicious.

139.s:
pārthive śasyasampattirativṛṣṭis tathā jayaḥ /
sarvajityuttamā vṛṣṭiḥ sarvadhārī subhikṣadaḥ //
139.d:
पार्थिवे शस्यसम्पत्तिरतिवृष्टिस् तथा जयः /
सर्वजित्युत्तमा वृष्टिः सर्वधारी सुभिक्षदः //
139.m:
In Pārthiva, there is abundance of crops, excessive rain, and victory.
In Sarvajit, there is excellent rain; Sarvadhārin grants abundance of food.

139.s:
virodhī jaladān hanti vikṛtaś ca bhayaṅkaraḥ /
khare bhavet pumān vīro nandane nandate prajā //
139.d:
विरोधी जलदान् हन्ति विकृतश् च भयङ्करः /
खरे भवेत् पुमान् वीरो नन्दने नन्दते प्रजा //
139.m:
Virodhin destroys the clouds, and Vikṛta is terrifying.
In Khara, a man becomes heroic; in Nandana, the people rejoice.

139.s:
viṣayaḥ śatruhantā ca śatrurogādi mardayet /
jvarārto manmathe loko duṣkare duṣkarā prajāḥ //
139.d:
विषयः शत्रुहन्ता च शत्रुरोगादि मर्दयेत् /
ज्वरार्तो मन्मथे लोको दुष्करे दुष्करा प्रजाः //
139.m:
Vijaya slays enemies and crushes enemies, diseases, and the like.
In Manmatha, the people are afflicted with fever; in Duṣkara, the subjects face hardship.

139.s:
durmukhe durmukho loko(1) hemalambe na sampadaḥ /
saṃvatsaro mahādevi vilambastu subhikṣadaḥ //
139.d:
दुर्मुखे दुर्मुखो लोको(1) हेमलम्बे न सम्पदः /
संवत्सरो महादेवि विलम्बस्तु सुभिक्षदः //
139.m:
In Durmukha, the people are foul-mouthed; in Hemalamba, there is no prosperity.
The year Vilamba, O great goddess, grants abundance of food.

139.s:
vikārī śatrukopāya vijaye sarvadā kvacit /
plave plavanti toyāni śobhane śubhakṛtprajā //
139.d:
विकारी शत्रुकोपाय विजये सर्वदा क्वचित् /
प्लवे प्लवन्ति तोयानि शोभने शुभकृत्प्रजा //
139.m:
Vikārin brings about the anger of enemies; in Vijaya, [victory is won] everywhere at times.
In Plava, waters overflow; in Śobhana, the people perform good deeds.

139.s:
rākṣase niṣṭhuro loko vividhandhānyamānane /
suvṛṣṭiḥ piṅgale kvāpi kāle hy ukto dhanakṣayaḥ //
139.d:
राक्षसे निष्ठुरो लोको विविधन्धान्यमानने /
सुवृष्टिः पिङ्गले क्वापि काले ह्य् उक्तो धनक्षयः //
139.m:
In Rākṣasa, people are cruel; in Ānanda, there are various grains.
In Piṅgala, there is good rain; in Kāla, loss of wealth is stated to occur.

139.s:
siddhārthe siddhyate sarvaṃ raudre raudraṃ pravartate /
durmatau madhyamā vṛṣṭirdundubhiḥ kṣemadhānyakṛt //
139.d:
सिद्धार्थे सिद्ध्यते सर्वं रौद्रे रौद्रं प्रवर्तते /
दुर्मतौ मध्यमा वृष्टिर्दुन्दुभिः क्षेमधान्यकृत् //
139.m:
In Siddhārtha, everything succeeds; in Raudra, dreadfulness prevails.
In Durmati, rain is moderate; Dundubhi produces security and grain.

139.s:
sravante rudhirodgārī raktākṣaḥ krodhane jayaḥ /
kṣaye kṣīṇadhano lokaḥ(2) ṣaṣṭisaṃvatsarāṇi tu //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave ṣaṣṭisaṃvatsarāṇi
nāma ūnacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 durmukhe mukhro loka iti kha.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
2 kṣīṇadhavo loka iti ka.. / kṣīṇajano loka iti ja..
:p 88
:ś atha catvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vaśyādiyogāḥ
139.d:
स्रवन्ते रुधिरोद्गारी रक्ताक्षः क्रोधने जयः /
क्षये क्षीणधनो लोकः(2) षष्टिसंवत्सराणि तु //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे षष्टिसंवत्सराणि
नाम ऊनचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 दुर्मुखे मुख्रो लोक इति ख.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
2 क्षीणधवो लोक इति क.. / क्षीणजनो लोक इति ज..
:प् 88
:श् अथ चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
वश्यादियोगाः
139.m:
In Rudhirodgārin, [wounds] flow; in Raktākṣa and Krodhana, there is victory.
In Kṣaya, people have diminished wealth. These are the sixty years.
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Sixty Years" in the Yuddhajayārṇava of the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1 "In Durmukha, people are loquacious" according to kha, gha, ṅa, and ña.
2 "People have lost husbands" according to ka. / "People are diminished in numbers" according to ja.
Now, the one hundred and fortieth chapter.
Formulas for Subjugation and Other Effects

140.s:
īśvara uvāca
vaśyādiyogān vakṣyāmi likhed dvyaṣṭapade tvimān /
bhṛṅgarājaḥ sahadevī(1) mayūrasya śikhā tathā //
140.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
वश्यादियोगान् वक्ष्यामि लिखेद् द्व्यष्टपदे त्विमान् /
भृङ्गराजः सहदेवी(1) मयूरस्य शिखा तथा //
140.m:
The Lord said:
I shall explain the formulas for subjugation and the like. One should draw these on a sixteen-square diagram:
Bhṛṅgarāja, sahadevī, and mayūraśikhā,

140.s:
putrañjīvakṛtañjalī hy adhaḥpuṣpā rudantikā /
kumārī rudrajaṭā(2) syādviṣṇukrāntā śito 'rkakaḥ //
140.d:
पुत्रञ्जीवकृतञ्जली ह्य् अधःपुष्पा रुदन्तिका /
कुमारी रुद्रजटा(2) स्याद्विष्णुक्रान्ता शितो ऽर्ककः //
140.m:
Putrañjīva, kṛtāñjali, adhaḥpuṣpā, rudantikā,
kumārī, rudrajaṭā, viṣṇukrāntā, white arka,

140.s:
lajjālukā mohalatā kṛṣṇadhustūrasañjñitā(3) /
gorakṣaḥ karkaṭo caiva meṣaśṛṅgī snuhī tathā //
140.d:
लज्जालुका मोहलता कृष्णधुस्तूरसञ्ज्ञिता(3) /
गोरक्षः कर्कटो चैव मेषशृङ्गी स्नुही तथा //
140.m:
Lajjālukā, mohalatā, the one named kṛṣṇadhustūra,
gorakṣa, karkaṭa, meṣaśṛṅgī, and snuhī.

140.s:
ṛtvijo 16 vahnaye 3 nāgāḥ 8 pakṣau 2 muni 3 manū 14 śivaḥ 11 /
vasavo 8 dik 10 rasā 6 vedā 4 graha 9 rtu6ravi 12 candramāḥ 1 //
140.d:
ऋत्विजो 16 वह्नये 3 नागाः 8 पक्षौ 2 मुनि 3 मनू 14 शिवः 11 /
वसवो 8 दिक् 10 रसा 6 वेदा 4 ग्रह 9 र्तु6रवि 12 चन्द्रमाः 1 //
140.m:
The officiating priests [16], fires [3], serpents [8], fortnights [2], sages [7], Manus [14], Śiva [11],
Vasuras [8], directions [10], tastes [6], Vedas [4], planets [9], seasons [6], suns [12], moon [1],

140.s:
tithayaś ca 15 kramādbhāgā oṣadhīnāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ /
prathamena catuṣkeṇa dhūpaścodvartanaṃ paraṃ //
140.d:
तिथयश् च 15 क्रमाद्भागा ओषधीनां प्रदक्षिणं /
प्रथमेन चतुष्केण धूपश्चोद्वर्तनं परं //
140.m:
And lunar days [15]—these are the divisions of herbs in order, clockwise.
With the first tetrad, incense and supreme unction [are made].

140.s:
tṛtīyenāñjanaṃ kuryāt snānaṃ kuryāccatuṣkataḥ /
bhṛṅgarājānulomācca caturdhā lepanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
140.d:
तृतीयेनाञ्जनं कुर्यात् स्नानं कुर्याच्चतुष्कतः /
भृङ्गराजानुलोमाच्च चतुर्धा लेपनं स्मृतं //
140.m:
With the third, one should make a collyrium; with the fourth tetrad, a bath.
In the regular order beginning with bhṛṅgarāja, an ointment is stated to be fourfold:

140.s:
munayo dakṣaṇe pārśve yugādyāścottarāḥ smṛtāḥ /
bhujagāḥ pādasaṃsthāś ca īśvarā mūrdhni saṃsthitāḥ //
140.d:
मुनयो दक्षणे पार्श्वे युगाद्याश्चोत्तराः स्मृताः /
भुजगाः पादसंस्थाश् च ईश्वरा मूर्ध्नि संस्थिताः //
140.m:
The sages are on the right side, the ages and their followers are on the left,
the serpents are placed at the feet, and the rulers are situated on the head.

140.s:
madhyena sārkaśaśibhirdhūpaḥ syāt sarvakāryake /
etair viliptadehastu tridaśair api pūjyate(4) //
:n
1 sahadevā iti kha.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. ca
2 kumārī vajrajaṭā iti cha..
3 kṛṣṇadhustūrasañjiketi kha..
4 tridaśair api gṛhyate iti gha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 89
140.d:
मध्येन सार्कशशिभिर्धूपः स्यात् सर्वकार्यके /
एतैर् विलिप्तदेहस्तु त्रिदशैर् अपि पूज्यते(4) //
:न्
1 सहदेवा इति ख.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. च
2 कुमारी वज्रजटा इति छ..
3 कृष्णधुस्तूरसञ्जिकेति ख..
4 त्रिदशैर् अपि गृह्यते इति घ.. , ङ.. च
:प् 89
140.m:
With the middle [herbs] together with the sun and moon, there should be incense for all purposes.
One whose body is anointed with these is worshipped even by the gods.
[Footnote]
1 "sahadevā" according to kha, gha, ṅa, and cha.
2 "kumārī vajrajaṭā" according to cha.
3 "kṛṣṇadhustūrasañjikā" according to kha.
4 "is accepted even by the gods" according to gha and ṅa.

140.s:
dhūpastu ṣoḍaśādyastu gṛhādyudvartane smṛtaḥ /
yugādyāścāñjane proktā vāṇādyāḥ snānakarmaṇi //
140.d:
धूपस्तु षोडशाद्यस्तु गृहाद्युद्वर्तने स्मृतः /
युगाद्याश्चाञ्जने प्रोक्ता वाणाद्याः स्नानकर्मणि //
140.m:
Incense beginning with the sixteenth is prescribed for smearing the house and so on.
Those beginning with the ages [four] are declared for collyrium, and those beginning with arrows [five] in the rite of bathing.

140.s:
rudrādyā bhakṣaṇe proktāḥ pakṣādyāḥ pānake smṛtāḥ /
ṛtvigvedartunayanaistilakaṃ lokamohanaṃ //
140.d:
रुद्राद्या भक्षणे प्रोक्ताः पक्षाद्याः पानके स्मृताः /
ऋत्विग्वेदर्तुनयनैस्तिलकं लोकमोहनं //
140.m:
Those beginning with Rudra [eleven] are declared for eating; those beginning with the wings [two] are taught for drinking.
With the officiating priests [16], Vedas [4], seasons [6], and eyes [2], a sectarian mark bewitches the world.

140.s:
sūryatridaśapakṣaiś ca śailaiḥ strī lepato vaśā /
candrendraphaṇirudraiś ca yonilepādvaśāḥ striyaḥ //
140.d:
सूर्यत्रिदशपक्षैश् च शैलैः स्त्री लेपतो वशा /
चन्द्रेन्द्रफणिरुद्रैश् च योनिलेपाद्वशाः स्त्रियः //
140.m:
With the suns [12], gods [13 or 3], wings [2], and mountains [7], a woman is subjugated by anointing.
With the moon [1], Indra [14], serpents [8], and Rudras [11], women are subjugated through vaginal anointment.

140.s:
tithidigyugavāṇaiś ca guṭikā tu vaśaṅkarī /
bhakṣye bhojye tathā pāne dātavyā guṭikā vaśe //
140.d:
तिथिदिग्युगवाणैश् च गुटिका तु वशङ्करी /
भक्ष्ये भोज्ये तथा पाने दातव्या गुटिका वशे //
140.m:
With the lunar days [15], directions [10], ages [4], and arrows [5], a pill causes subjugation;
in food, solid nourishment, and drink, the pill should be given for subjugation.

140.s:
ṛtviggrahākṣiśailaiś ca śastrastambhe mukhe dhṛtā /
śailendravedarandhraiś ca aṅgalepājjale vaset //
140.d:
ऋत्विग्ग्रहाक्षिशैलैश् च शस्त्रस्तम्भे मुखे धृता /
शैलेन्द्रवेदरन्ध्रैश् च अङ्गलेपाज्जले वसेत् //
140.m:
Held in the mouth with [herbs of] priests [16], planets [9], eyes [2], and mountains [7], weapons are paralyzed.
With the mountains [7], Indra [14], Vedas [4], and openings [9], one can dwell in water by anointing the limbs.

140.s:
vāṇākṣimanurudraiś ca guṭikā kṣuttṛṣādinut /
triṣoḍaśadiśāvāṇair lepāt strī durbhagā śubhā //
140.d:
वाणाक्षिमनुरुद्रैश् च गुटिका क्षुत्तृषादिनुत् /
त्रिषोडशदिशावाणैर् लेपात् स्त्री दुर्भगा शुभा //
140.m:
With arrows [5], eyes [2], Manus [14], and Rudras [11], a pill dispels hunger, thirst, and the like.
Through anointing with [the herbs of] the three, sixteen, directions [10], and arrows [5], an unfortunate woman becomes auspicious.

140.s:
tridaśākṣidiśānetrair lepāt krīḍecca patragaiḥ /
tridaśākṣeśabhujagair lepāt strī sūyate sukhaṃ //
140.d:
त्रिदशाक्षिदिशानेत्रैर् लेपात् क्रीडेच्च पत्रगैः /
त्रिदशाक्षेशभुजगैर् लेपात् स्त्री सूयते सुखं //
140.m:
Through anointment with the gods [13 or 3], eyes [2], directions [10], and eyes [2], one can play with birds.
Through anointment with the gods [13 or 3], eyes [2], the Lord [11], and serpents [8], a woman gives birth with ease.

140.s:
saptadiṅmunirandhraiś ca dyūtajihvastralepataḥ /
tridaśākṣyabdhimunibhirdhvajalepāt(1) ratau sutaḥ //
140.d:
सप्तदिङ्मुनिरन्ध्रैश् च द्यूतजिह्वस्त्रलेपतः /
त्रिदशाक्ष्यब्धिमुनिभिर्ध्वजलेपात्(1) रतौ सुतः //
140.m:
Through anointing the gaming dice with the seven, directions [10], sages [7], and openings [9], [victory is won].
Through anointing the phallus with the gods [13 or 3], eyes [2], oceans [4], and sages [7], a son is born in intercourse.

140.s:
grahābdhisarpyatridaśair guṭikā syād vaśaṅkarī /
ṛtvikpadasthitauṣadhyāḥ prabhāvaḥ pratipāditaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave ṣoḍaśapadakā nāma
catvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 tridaśākṣyandhimanubhirdhvajalepāditi ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. ca
:p 90
:ś athaikacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṣaṭtriṃśatpadakajñānaṃ
140.d:
ग्रहाब्धिसर्प्यत्रिदशैर् गुटिका स्याद् वशङ्करी /
ऋत्विक्पदस्थितौषध्याः प्रभावः प्रतिपादितः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे षोडशपदका नाम
चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 त्रिदशाक्ष्यन्धिमनुभिर्ध्वजलेपादिति ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. च
:प् 90
:श् अथैकचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
षट्त्रिंशत्पदकज्ञानं
140.m:
With the planets [9], oceans [4], serpents [8], and gods [13 or 3], there is a subjugating pill.
The power of the herbs placed in the squares of the priests has thus been expounded.
Thus ends the one hundred and fortieth chapter, entitled "The Sixteen-Square Diagram" in the Yuddhajayārṇava of the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1 "tridaśākṣyandhimanubhirdhvajalepāt" according to ga, gha, ṅa, and cha.
Now, the one hundred and forty-first chapter.
Knowledge of the Thirty-Six Square Diagram

141.s:
īśvara uvāca
ṣaṭtriṃśatpadasaṃsthānāmoṣadhīnāṃ vade phalaṃ /
amarīkaraṇaṃ nṛṇāṃ brahmarudrendrasevitaṃ //
141.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
षट्त्रिंशत्पदसंस्थानामोषधीनां वदे फलं /
अमरीकरणं नृणां ब्रह्मरुद्रेन्द्रसेवितं //
141.m:
The Lord said:
I shall state the fruit of the herbs situated in the thirty-six squares,
which makes mortals immortal, worshipped by Brahmā, Rudra, and Indra:

141.s:
harītakyakṣyadhātrāś ca marīcampippalīśiphā /
vahniḥ śuṇṭhī pippalī ca guḍūcīvacanimbakāḥ(1) //
141.d:
हरीतक्यक्ष्यधात्राश् च मरीचम्पिप्पलीशिफा /
वह्निः शुण्ठी पिप्पली च गुडूचीवचनिम्बकाः(1) //
141.m:
Harītakī, akṣa, dhātrī, marīca, pippalī-root,
vahni, ginger, pippalī, guḍūcī, vacā, and nimba,

141.s:
vāsakaḥ śatamūlī ca saindhavaṃ sindhuvārakaṃ /
kaṇṭakārī gokṣurakā vilvampaunarnavaṃ balā //
141.d:
वासकः शतमूली च सैन्धवं सिन्धुवारकं /
कण्टकारी गोक्षुरका विल्वम्पौनर्नवं बला //
141.m:
Vāsaka, śatamūlī, rock salt, sindhuvāra,
kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura, bilva, punarnavā, and balā,

141.s:
eraṇḍamuṇḍī rucako bhṛṅgaḥ kṣāro 'tha parpaṭaḥ /
dhanyāko jīrakaś caiva śatapuṣyī javānikā //
141.d:
एरण्डमुण्डी रुचको भृङ्गः क्षारो ऽथ पर्पटः /
धन्याको जीरकश् चैव शतपुष्यी जवानिका //
141.m:
Eraṇḍa, muṇḍī, rucaka, bhṛṅga, alkali, and parpaṭa,
coriander, cumin, śatapuṣpā, javānikā,

141.s:
viḍaṅgaḥ khadiraś caiva kṛtamālo haridrayā /
vacā siddhārtha etāni ṣaṭtriṃśatpadagāni hi //
141.d:
विडङ्गः खदिरश् चैव कृतमालो हरिद्रया /
वचा सिद्धार्थ एतानि षट्त्रिंशत्पदगानि हि //
141.m:
Viḍaṅga, khadira, kṛtamāla with haridrā,
vacā, and white mustard—these are located in the thirty-six squares.

141.s:
kramādekādisañjñāni hy aupadhāni mahānti hi /
sarvarogaharāṇi syuramarīkaraṇāni ca //
141.d:
क्रमादेकादिसञ्ज्ञानि ह्य् औपधानि महान्ति हि /
सर्वरोगहराणि स्युरमरीकरणानि च //
141.m:
Designated by numbers from one onwards in order, these are great medicinal plants.
They remove all diseases and confer immortality,

141.s:
balīpalitabhettṝṇi(2) sarvakoṣṭhagatāni tu /
eṣāṃ cūrṇañca vaṭikā rasena paribhāvitā //
141.d:
बलीपलितभेत्तॄणि(2) सर्वकोष्ठगतानि तु /
एषां चूर्णञ्च वटिका रसेन परिभाविता //
141.m:
Destroying wrinkles and grey hair, and reaching every organ.
A powder of these, or a pill macerated in juice,

141.s:
avalehaḥ kaṣāyo vā modako guḍakhaṇḍakaḥ /
:n
1 cavyanimbakā iti ja.. , jha.. ca
2 balīpalitabhedīnīti cha..
:p 91
madhuto dhṛtato vāpi ghṛtantailamathāpi vā //
141.d:
अवलेहः कषायो वा मोदको गुडखण्डकः /
:न्
1 चव्यनिम्बका इति ज.. , झ.. च
2 बलीपलितभेदीनीति छ..
:प् 91
मधुतो धृततो वापि घृतन्तैलमथापि वा //
141.m:
An electuary, a decoction, a sweet ball, or a jaggery preparation,
[Footnote]
1 "cavyanimbakāḥ" according to ja and jha.
2 "balīpalitabhedīni" according to cha.
Taken with honey or ghee, or clarified butter or oil,

141.s:
sarvātmanopayuktaṃ hi mṛtasañjīvanambhavet /
karṣārdhaṃ karṣamekaṃ vā palārdhaṃ palamekakaṃ //
141.d:
सर्वात्मनोपयुक्तं हि मृतसञ्जीवनम्भवेत् /
कर्षार्धं कर्षमेकं वा पलार्धं पलमेककं //
141.m:
Consumed by all means, it becomes a reviver of the dead.
[Taken in the measure of] half a karṣa, one karṣa, half a pala, or one pala,

141.s:
yatheṣṭācāranirato(1) jīvedvarṣaśatatrayaṃ /
mṛtasañjīvanīkalpe yogo nāsmāt paro 'sti hi //
141.d:
यथेष्टाचारनिरतो(1) जीवेद्वर्षशतत्रयं /
मृतसञ्जीवनीकल्पे योगो नास्मात् परो ऽस्ति हि //
141.m:
One who indulges in whatever conduct he pleases will live for three hundred years.
In the practice of reviving the dead, there is indeed no formula superior to this.

141.s:
prathamānnavakādyogāt sarvarogaiḥ pramucyate /
dvitīyācca tṛtīyācca caturthānmucyate rujaḥ //
141.d:
प्रथमान्नवकाद्योगात् सर्वरोगैः प्रमुच्यते /
द्वितीयाच्च तृतीयाच्च चतुर्थान्मुच्यते रुजः //
141.m:
From the formula of the first group of nine, one is freed from all diseases;
from the second, third, and fourth [groups of nine], one is freed from sickness.

141.s:
evaṃ ṣaṭkācca prathamād dvitīyācca tṛtīyataḥ /
caturthātpañcamāt ṣaṣṭhāttathā navacatuṣkataḥ //
141.d:
एवं षट्काच्च प्रथमाद् द्वितीयाच्च तृतीयतः /
चतुर्थात्पञ्चमात् षष्ठात्तथा नवचतुष्कतः //
141.m:
Likewise from the first group of six, the second, the third,
the fourth, fifth, and sixth; and similarly from the four groups of nine.
[One is freed] from wind [humour] by the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth; / and from bile by the fire (three), sun (twelve), twenty-sixth, and twenty-seventh;

141.s:
vāṇartuśailavasubhistithibhirmucyate kaphāt /
vedāgnibhirbāṇaguṇaiḥ ṣadguṇaiḥ syādvaśe dhṛte //
141.d:
वाणर्तुशैलवसुभिस्तिथिभिर्मुच्यते कफात् /
वेदाग्निभिर्बाणगुणैः षद्गुणैः स्याद्वशे धृते //
141.m: from phlegm one is freed by the arrows (five), seasons (six), mountains (seven), Vasus (eight), and tithi (fifteen). / By the Vedas (four) and fire (three), arrows (five) and qualities (three), and six and qualities (three), [the enemy] will be brought under control.

141.s:
grahādigrahaṇāntaiś ca sarvair eva vimucyate /
ekadvitrirasaiḥ śailair vasugrahaśivaiḥ kramāt //
141.d:
ग्रहादिग्रहणान्तैश् च सर्वैर् एव विमुच्यते /
एकद्वित्रिरसैः शैलैर् वसुग्रहशिवैः क्रमात् //
141.m: And by all those beginning with planets (nine) and ending with eclipses, one is entirely liberated. / In order, by one, two, three, tastes (six), mountains (seven), Vasus (eight), planets (nine), Śivas (eleven),

141.s:
dvātriṃśattithisūryaiś ca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
ṣaṭtriṃśatpadakajñānaṃ na deyaṃ yasya kasya cit //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yuddhajayārṇave
ṣaṭtriṃśatpadakajñānaṃ nāma ekacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 yathecchācāranirata iti ja..
:p 92
:ś atha dvicatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mantroṣadhādiḥ
141.d:
द्वात्रिंशत्तिथिसूर्यैश् च नात्र कार्या विचारणा /
षट्त्रिंशत्पदकज्ञानं न देयं यस्य कस्य चित् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे युद्धजयार्णवे
षट्त्रिंशत्पदकज्ञानं नाम एकचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 यथेच्छाचारनिरत इति ज..
:प् 92
:श् अथ द्विचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
मन्त्रोषधादिः
141.m:
thirty-two, tithis (fifteen), and suns (twelve)—no doubt should be entertained here. / This knowledge of thirty-six squares must not be given to just anyone.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, in the 'Ocean of Victory in Battle', the one hundred and forty-first chapter, entitled 'Knowledge of the Thirty-Six Squares'.
[Footnote]
[Notes to page 92]
Now the one hundred and forty-second chapter.
Mantras, Herbs, and Other [Remedies]

142.s:
īśvara uvāca
mantrauṣadhāni cakrāṇi(1) vakṣye sarvapradāni ca /
cauranāmno varṇaguṇo dvighno mātrāś caturguṇāḥ //
142.d:
ईश्वर उवाच
मन्त्रौषधानि चक्राणि(1) वक्ष्ये सर्वप्रदानि च /
चौरनाम्नो वर्णगुणो द्विघ्नो मात्राश् चतुर्गुणाः //
142.m: The Lord said: / I shall declare the diagrams of mantras and herbs that grant all desires. / The letters of a thief's name multiplied by three and doubled, and the morae multiplied by four,

142.s:
nāmnā hṛte bhaveccheṣadyauro 'tha jātakaṃ vade /
praśne ye viṣamā varṇāste garbhe putrajanmadāḥ //
142.d:
नाम्ना हृते भवेच्छेषद्यौरो ऽथ जातकं वदे /
प्रश्ने ये विषमा वर्णास्ते गर्भे पुत्रजन्मदाः //
142.m: when divided by the name, the remainder will reveal the thief. Now I declare the nativity: / In divination, the odd syllables indicate the birth of a son in the womb;

142.s:
nāmavarṇaiḥ samaiḥ kāṇo vāme 'kṣṇi viṣamaiḥ punaḥ /
dakṣiṇākṣi bhavet kāṇaṃ strīpunnāmākṣarasya ca //
142.d:
नामवर्णैः समैः काणो वामे ऽक्ष्णि विषमैः पुनः /
